# BANNERWAKE ALL NPC AND DIALOGUE XML REFERENCE FOR CLAUDE

Generated from the local Bannerlord install on 2026-06-04.
Correction pass applied on 2026-06-05 against local beta v1.4.5 + NavalDLC.



This document indexes every official `NPCCharacter` and `Hero` XML record found in the scoped vanilla plus War Sails/NavalDLC files. It also indexes every base non-localization `<string>` record in the official modules, while marking the core dialogue, lore, voice/persona, comment, trait, wanderer, StoryMode, and War Sails dialogue pools separately from UI/general strings.

Important limitation: Bannerlord's XML does not attach every possible spoken line directly to every NPC. Dialogue selection is tag-driven and code-driven: voice/persona, register, trait reputation, relationship, encounter state, battle/sea state, quest state, and StoryMode logic choose from shared string pools. For that reason, this file gives Claude a full state/tag/string-ID map with short identifying snippets, not a verbatim transcript dump of all game dialogue.

## Companion Backstory Dialogue
*Source: `SandBox/ModuleData/companion_strings.xml` — 256 entries*

**str_npc_intro.1** — Greetings, wanderer. Might I know where you are from?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.1** — Oh, here and there. I'm a recent arrival in Calradia.

**str_npc_intro_response_2.1** — Mind your own business, mate.

**str_npc_backstory_a.1** — Ah, a pity. If you were a native of Calradia, I would be most interested to know about your ancestry and some particulars of your place of birth. I am collecting notes on the lineages of this land, both of the great imperial families and of our barbarian brethren.

**str_npc_backstory_b.1** — I confess I find the barbarians particularly interesting, for they have many virtues that we in the Empire have lost - a certain honesty of spirit, I should say, not our thick stew of civilized intrigues.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.1** — Yes. Please continue.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.1** — All very interesting to a scholar, I suppose, but not to me. Good day.

**str_npc_backstory_d.1** — If you are a wanderer, as you say, perhaps it would be to my advantage to go along with you, to collect such stories as I can. I may indeed be able to assist you in some way.

**str_npc_backstory_later.1** — I've been about, in halls and gers and tents, collecting some fascinating accounts. But I'd still be interested in accompanying you, if you'll have me.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.1** — Perhaps. What skills do you have to offer?

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.1** — I'm most interested in the barbarian virtue of sticking axes in skulls. You don't look the type.

**str_npc_signup.1** — I can offer you my knowledge of the ancestries of the lords, chieftains, noyans, and other nobility of Calradia, both civilized and savage. You will find that it may please them if you claim to recognize, on first making their acquaintance, the name of their clan, and whether they are called 'The Boneless,' 'Nestbeard,' 'The Scratcher,' or some other charming sobriquet.

**str_npc_signup_2.1** — The one thing I ask - other than food, shelter, and a few denars for pocket expenses, of course - is that I am not party to pillage and slave-taking.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.1** — Very well. Consider yourself hired.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.1** — I don't take recruits who impose conditions on me. Good day to you.

**str_npc_payment.1** — Splendid, {?PLAYER.GENDER}madame{?}sir{\?}! There is one other small favor. I have incurred a few debts in this town, mostly due to the spilling of wine upon books. I would ask for an advance of {NPCPAYMENT} on my pay.

**str_npc_payment_response.1** — Very well, here's {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}.

**str_npc_intro.2** — Aye?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.2** — Greetings. I'm looking for warriors, and you look like you might fit the bill.

**str_npc_intro_response_2.2** — Never mind.

**str_npc_backstory_a.2** — You might say that. I've served in the empire's legions for two decades. Once upon a time they were worthy of being called 'legions.' We served together for years, the same group of men under a single standard, and we'd die rather than see those standards falter or fall. But Drosios Neretzes led the last of the real legions into an ambush in the Battanian woods. You may have heard that story.

**str_npc_backstory_b.2** — I blame Arenicos and his so-called reforms. It saved him silver, but now our armies are just blown-up lords' retinues - toadies, farmers who have no business on the battlefield, a few good men but not enough. There's no pride and no discipline. No wonder that we're squabbling among ourselves these days, being mocked by the barbarians we used to rule.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.2** — Ah, the old days. And no doubt back then they complained about the older days. I've heard enough.

**str_npc_backstory_d.2** — But maybe it's for the best. Whoever wins this war will at least be a worth leader of men.... Are you're looking for swords to hire? I'm bored and I'm ready to jump into the game again, and I doubt my wife will miss me much.

**str_npc_backstory_later.2** — I've been around and about. I'm still bored. I'm still drinking more than I should.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.2** — I have a band of fighters, and I could use a man with some experience.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.2** — ....

**str_npc_signup.2** — That's good to hear. Naturally I expect to be compensated in silver for my blood and sweat.

**str_npc_signup_2.2** — In return for that, I promise to do my best to whip whatever sorry rabble you recruit into soldiers. I don't bother with horsemen and I don't bother with bowmen. But give me footmen with a bit of guts, and I'll teach them to stand together in a rock-solid formation that will break any charge you care to throw at it.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.2** — I think I could use a man like you.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.2** — Actually, I'm more interested in skirmishers.

**str_npc_payment.2** — Splendid - about the money. Shall we say an advance of {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}? That's enough for me to know you're serious.

**str_npc_payment_response.2** — Very well, here's {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}.

**str_npc_intro.3** — Greeting, {?PLAYER.GENDER}madame{?}sir{\?}. Are you by any chance in the market for an engineer?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.3** — I might be. What do you have to offer?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.3** — No, I'm not, I'm afraid. Good day to you.

**str_npc_backstory_a.3** — I hope you don't mind a little immodesty. If you're building, I'm one of the best you can hire. I can build any arch, any tower, any dome you might want. Every city around here has examples of my craft.

**str_npc_backstory_b.3** — If you're knocking down, I'm not just one of the best - I am the best. I do rams, mines, and of course catapults. Torsion and counterweight. You can ask any castellan in any town in Calradia... Well, maybe best not ask in this town, but any other town in Calradia.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.3** — I see. What happened here?

**str_npc_interrupt_2.3** — You do not inspire me with confidence.

**str_npc_backstory_d.3** — Well, the master of artillery here took the counterweight right on the skull. It was a 5-pound ball, so the counterweight weighed about as much as a small horse. You can imagine what that looked like. So they're not going to pay me - even though the ball, I'm proud to say, threw straight over 500 paces. Even with a bit of muck on it.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.3** — That's very impressive! From a technical standpoint, that is.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.3** — Above all, an engineer must be cautious. Good-day, sir.

**str_npc_signup.3** — At any rate, I got out of there when they were still bumbling about with a bucket and mop. But if there's an inquiry and people start looking for someone to blame, well, they'll probably decide to point the finger at the external contractor. So I wouldn't mind getting out of town.

**str_npc_signup_2.3** — Take me on now, and you can have my services for a fraction of what they're worth. Believe me, in your line of work, there's no bigger expense than a lengthy siege. Unless you like drinking dirty water and squatting in muddy ditches, hiring me is an opportunity you can't afford to miss.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.3** — I can't pass up a bargain like that. I'd like to hire you.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.3** — You try too hard to sell yourself. I guess I'm going to have to say 'no.'.

**str_npc_payment.3** — Excellent. I'd like an advance payment, not least because I'm going to need to get my equipment cleanred. Shall we say {NPCPAYMENT}?

**str_npc_payment_response.3** — Very well, here's {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}.

**str_npc_intro.4** — Yes? I'll have you know, I'm not normally in the habit of talking to strangers in taverns.

**str_npc_intro_response_1.4** — I find it a good way of picking up useful information.

**str_npc_intro_response_2.4** — In that case, I shall go bother someone else.

**str_npc_backstory_a.4** — Ah yes, I suppose it is. Well, if it interests you, my name is Haldaea, and I have resolved to become a warrior.

**str_npc_backstory_b.4** — I'm sure it has not escaped you that this empire of ours is in a dreadful state. Men have lost all sense of duty and self-respect, and regularly turn their tail in the face of rebels, barbarians, and other such rabble.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.4** — Sorry times indeed, madame. Pray continue.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.4** — Rabble? Barbarians? These are my friends you're talking about!

**str_npc_backstory_d.4** — I intend to find the captain of a company who will take me on as an apprentice. I will thereupon master the arts of war, and raise a company of my own, and thus shame the males of the empire into recovering their lost manhood.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.4** — Well, you have the right attitude. I might take you on.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.4** — I think you are wasting your time, madame. Good day

**str_npc_signup.4** — If you do so, I promise to always be in the front rank of your battle line, to never shirk duty even in the face of death.

**str_npc_signup_2.4** — I will ensure that your men fear my scorn more than they do the spears of the enemy.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.4** — Splendid. That's the spirit. Gather your belongings.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.4** — Scorn alone does not make men brave, madame. I think you'd best find another captain.

**str_npc_payment.4** — Splendid. I will need a small amount of money in advance - {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}. I have several servants, who have been with our family for years, who cannot accompany me. Honor and basic humanity require that I give them a small amount of money to get on their feet.

**str_npc_payment_response.4** — Very well, here's {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}.

**str_npc_intro.6** — Ho there. Will you join me in a cup of ale?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.6** — Very well. Here's to your health.

**str_npc_intro_response_2.6** — I am otherwise occupied, sir.

**str_npc_backstory_a.6** — And to your health, both physical and spiritual! And always remember - spiritual health comes only from repentence, and for that you have need of something to repent.

**str_npc_backstory_b.6** — I'll grant that's a bit of a heretical notion to the imperial priesthood, but then I was raised a heretic. Perhaps you've heard of the Embers of the Flame? Well, I was born into the retinue of a Perfect, back when the Embers were blazing fire and we wandered the countryside preaching faith and rebellion.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.6** — Go on.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.6** — This conversation got rather dangerous rather quickly.

**str_npc_backstory_c.6** — I reckon I had a gift for a sermon. We'd wander into a village and I'd cut loose with a speech that would have the villagers selling their lands and joining us on our endless pilgrimage. But you know, I suppose the Perfect got a little jealous, started accusing me of deadly error here and the sin of pride there...

**str_npc_backstory_d.6** — It got tiresome, I can tell you, being accused of heresy by a heretic while living on donations by day and hiding in the hedgerows at night lest the local nobility got tired of us coaxing their tenants into holy poverty. I told the Perfect I wished to bring our message to the towns, and he gave me leave to come here, but I reckon I've gone a little bit astray.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.6** — The Heavens lead us where they will. And how do you make your living?

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.6** — A colorful life, I suppose, but of little interest to me. Good day to you.

**str_npc_signup.6** — So, then... I've had odd jobs for the past few years. Mostly I stand in marketplaces shouting out the virtues of this one's saddles or that one's melons...

**str_npc_signup_2.6** — But suppose I found an ambitious young captain - perhaps someone like your good self, someone who needed to sway a crowd or inspire soldiers at some point. I reckon I could travel with that captain - sharing all the battles and hardships of the road, of course - and perhaps teach them a bit of what I know.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.6** — I might be able to hire someone like that.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.6** — My apologies, but that is not of interest to me.

**str_npc_payment.6** — Splendid! Ah, but before I sign on... A few of the girls working in this tavern... Well, on the off-chance I've left one or two of them with child, I should leave a bit of coin with them before I go. {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} should cover it. Can you advance me that?

**str_npc_payment_response.6** — If that's your last 'last request,' I suppose I can. Here's {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}.

**str_npc_intro.7** — Hello. Come any closer and I'll stick a knife in your belly, but if you remain where you are, I see no reason not to have a pleasant chat.

**str_npc_intro_response_1.7** — I'll stand where I am. So, why so friendly a greeting?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.7** — I'm backing away now, lady. Good day to you.

**str_npc_backstory_a.7** — Well, there was a time when I was less wary of strangers, but I've learned since that many of those who approach me in an inn or on the road have unworthy motives. It's a bit of a tale, but I will tell you if you're interested.

**str_npc_backstory_b.7** — I had a bit of a protected upbringing, you see. I am a great-niece of Aldric, lord of Sarghert. My father died in his wars, but I was considered a member of his household, and I was to be married to a horseman in his retinue. Alas, I fell in love with one of the common soldiers. He was high-spirited, handsome - the kind of boy who imagined the evils of this world could never touch him.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.7** — Go on.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.7** — Never mind.

**str_npc_backstory_d.7** — I fled Sarghert. In a tavern in Bostrum, I found myself a surgeon who agreed to take me on as apprentice. I followed the empire's armies, and I found that my knowledge learned in the barracks of Sarghert had a use. I became a surgeon's apprentice, removing arrows from ribcages or trepanning a skull.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.7** — A sad tale, my dear, but Calradia is full of them. Good day.

**str_npc_signup.7** — I am.

**str_npc_intro.8** — Hello, stranger. 'The cat walks on silent paws.'

**str_npc_intro_response_1.8** — Uh, 'but carries a large bird in its mouth'?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.8** — You must have me confused with someone else.

**str_npc_backstory_a.8** — Nice try, stranger. That's not the other half of the callword. But you don't look like the city watch, so I'm going to take a little risk here and ask you something.

**str_npc_backstory_b.8** — Are you heading out of town? I've been here for three days waiting for my contact to show up, but I don't think he will. I suspect that I might have drawn a bit of attention to myself.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.8** — I might be heading out of town. Tell me a little more about yourself.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.8** — Then the last thing I want, my lady, is to be seen talking to you.

**str_npc_backstory_d.8** — As you can guess, I'm a smuggler. And a good one, at that.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.8** — Well, that's upfront of you to tell me that. What skills would you bring to my company?

**str_npc_signup.8** — My parents moved to Baravenus as refugees from Sturgian raids, and I started off doing errands for the merchants. Some of them like to get merchandise in or out of the city without going through the gate - they don't care for paying tariffs, perhaps, or maybe the item's original owner is out looking for it.

**str_npc_signup_2.8** — So, in time, I made contacts in towns up and down the western half of Calradia. Sometimes it's a guard who's not averse to a little extra cash. Sometimes there's a washerwoman who'll let down a rope over the walls at night. Is that the knowledge that's useful to you?

**str_npc_signup_response_1.8** — That is useful. Can you also fight?

**str_npc_signup_response_2.8** — I'm afraid not, my lady. You'd best leave now.

**str_npc_payment.8** — Oh, have no fear. I don't swat down armies like flies but I can probably take them down one or two villains at a time, if need be. There is, however, a small matter of asking you for - {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}. I have run up a bit of a tab at this tavern, and I may need to use it again at some point.

**str_npc_intro.9** — Hello, wanderer. Care to join me for a cup of wine?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.9** — No harm in that, I suppose. So. Tell me about yourself.

**str_npc_intro_response_2.9** — I am otherwise occupied, sir.

**str_npc_backstory_a.9** — I am Tabur son of Alqan. You do not recognize the name? Well, perhaps we move in different circles. Any connoisseur of dinner parties, wine, courtesans, and poetry would doubtless have heard of me.

**str_npc_backstory_b.9** — Why, just the other evening I was attending a soiree in this very town, and the host told me that I was truly an ornament among guests, who brought more light to his party than a hundred lanterns, more music than a hundred lutes. It was with great sorrow, he said, that he must call his guards on me, because by some oversight I had not been invited and thus in eating his food I was, by a legal technicality, a thief.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.9** — How blunt of him! What happened next?

**str_npc_interrupt_2.9** — And he was right to say that! Good day. sir.

**str_npc_backstory_d.9** — I confess that this is not the first time something like this has happened to me. Hosts can be such sticklers about their guest lists. But it has left me at a bit of an impasse, as I should probably leave this town sooner rather than later.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.9** — So you live by sneaking into other men's dinner parties, I see. But it sounds like you have a useful set of skills.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.9** — You sound like trouble, sir. Good day.

**str_npc_signup.9** — My friend, why should a man not eat the finest food off of golden plates, if he has the wit to do so? Although I confess I am growing a bit jaded of it all, and perhaps would enjoy a change of pace.

**str_npc_signup_2.9** — More importantly, I really should be moving on. I don't suppose you might be in the market for my talents and knowledge? I know a back door into every city in the eastern half of Calradia, or the right guard to bribe.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.9** — Very well. That could come in handy. I can offer you a place in my company.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.9** — I have no golden plates for you to dine off. I doubt you'd last long with us. Good day to you.

**str_npc_payment.9** — Splendid! I must ask you, however, for a small downpayment of {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}. I have a debt that I had hoped to repay with some silverware, but I encountered some difficulties with that.

**str_npc_intro.10** — Do you know who I am, traveler?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.10** — No, can't say that I do. So who are you?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.10** — I do not know, nor do I care to.

**str_npc_backstory_a.10** — The searing gravel plain knows me, as do the rippling sands and the shadowed canyon. I have faced the scouring sandstorm, the rushing flood, the killing heat of noontime, and they have all said to me, 'Pass safely, brother.'

**str_npc_backstory_b.10** — I am Lath, prince of the wastelands, lord of solitude, master of emptiness. If you wish to know my other names, you may ask my kinsmen, the leopard, the hyena and the gazelle.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.10** — Lath is fine. No need to speak to the hyenas. What do you do?

**str_npc_interrupt_2.10** — Master of empty talk, rather. Good day, sir.

**str_npc_backstory_d.10** — However, although the desert is bountiful, horses and steel must be bought with silver. So, I wish to inform you, my services are for hire.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.10** — Hmm. I could be interested. What can you offer me?

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.10** — I have no interest in your services.

**str_npc_signup.10** — I am a pathfinder and a scout.

**str_npc_signup_2.10** — If you wish to pass swiftly through the desert, to find shelters to hide from your foes, to find water where others find only dust and death, then I am your man.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.10** — Very well, I can offer you a place in my company.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.10** — Perhaps at a later date.

**str_npc_payment.10** — You will not regret your decision. One thing I must ask - before riding out, I need a new bridle and saddle. An advance of {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} should suffice.

**str_npc_intro.11** — There is only one thing that I want to hear from anyone right now: that the news I have heard is false. That the warehouse in Makeb which I stored my pepper did not catch fire, and that I have not lost my fortune.

**str_npc_intro_response_1.11** — You invested your whole fortune in a single cargo of pepper?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.11** — I've heard bad luck is contagious. Good-bye.

**str_npc_backstory_a.11** — I did. Well, it was a risk - but a calculated one. If you are willing to listen to my story, I would welcome the chance to unburden my sorrows.

**str_npc_backstory_b.11** — My father was a merchant. When he died, he left his children a small inheritance. Most went to my brothers. They headed east, to the lands of the Padishah, leaving me in charge of our interests in Calradia. For me to step into my father's shoes, and be treated as an equal by other merchants, I knew I had to make a lot of money in a short time or they would elbow me out of the market.

**str_npc_backstory_d.11** — Even now I feel I made a wise choice to buy the pepper -- wise, but unlucky. Such is fortune! Had I not seized this opportunity, other merchants would have mocked me, a woman too timid to succeed in a man's trade. Now they tut-tut, a rash woman who lacked a man's judgment.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.11** — If you know your way around caravans, I may have some work for you.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.11** — A wise king once said: I ask only of my generals that they be lucky. Good day, madame.

**str_npc_signup.11** — I do indeed. I pay attention to packing and loading in particular. It is a fine art, one which determines how fast a beast of burden can move, whether a caravan makes good time or is forever pausing to pick up a spilled load.

**str_npc_signup_2.11** — If you carry many supplies, I can promise you -- as much as anyone can promise anything, in this uncertain world -- that I will repay my salary many times over.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.11** — Splendid. I have every confidence in you.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.11** — That is too specialized a skill, my lady. Good-bye.

**str_npc_payment.11** — There is only one thing I must ask. I would like to leave this town with clean balance books. I would like to settle all my debts. An advance of {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} should be enough.

**str_npc_intro.12** — I'm here to drink, not to talk, so whatever it you have to say, I'd advise you to say it to someone else. Unless, that is, you have a fight that needs fighting.

**str_npc_intro_response_1.12** — Uh, well, I might. Why would you want to fight for me?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.12** — If I did, I'd be inclined to seek the services of someone less foul-tempered.

**str_npc_backstory_a.12** — Why? I'll tell you why.

**str_npc_backstory_b.12** — Because I've drunk my way through all the silver in my pocket, and I'm thirsty again. Because it's been a too long since I swung a sword, and my arm's a bit itchy. Because if you don't kill a man every few weeks, people forget what you're about. There. You need only one reason, and I just give you three.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.12** — You sound like you have the right attitude. Tell me more about yourself.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.12** — I like my men to be aggressive, but there are limits. Good-day, sir.

**str_npc_backstory_d.12** — I hope I've made it clear to you what I'm about.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.12** — Very well. One thing I can promise you is a lot of fighting.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.12** — ...

**str_npc_signup.12** — Here's my conditions: I expect to be paid well, and I don't kill men who don't fight back.

**str_npc_signup_2.12** — In return, I promise you I'll be first into every battle. I also yell a lot. You'll find it encourages the others. Do we have a deal?

**str_npc_signup_response_1.12** — Sure. I suppose we do.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.12** — Let me think about this a bit.

**str_npc_payment.12** — Good. I'm going to want from you {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} up front. Like I say, I'm a thirsty man.

**str_npc_intro.13** — Greetings, stranger. You must be a stranger here, for few born here would speak to me.

**str_npc_intro_response_1.13** — And why is that? What's your story?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.13** — They must know something I do not. Good day, my lady.

**str_npc_backstory_a.13** — When I was a girl, I chose to be a shieldmaiden, and accompanied my brothers on their raids. When I came of age, I was pursued by one of the finest warriors in our valley. All the girls dreamed of marrying him. I agreed to marry him on condition that he never tried to prevent me from going to war, and this pledge he made.

**str_npc_backstory_b.13** — Soon into our marriage he lost his ardor for me, and began to regret his pledge. When I sought to go raiding, he scowled and demanded that I stay home and give him children. He became jealous. When I cursed him back, he struck me with the flat of his sword. One day, in the marketplace, before all the people of our village, he accused me of lying with anyone who crossed my path, man or woman. I struck him. By the laws of our people he had not given me any grounds for divorce, so I demanded a fight to the death instead.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.13** — That is one solution to a bad marriage. Did you go through with this plan?

**str_npc_interrupt_2.13** — You dueled your husband? Heavens avert all evil. I have heard enough.

**str_npc_backstory_d.13** — He fought to kill, but I was faster, and I slew him. I feel no regret. Let any man who imagines he can treat a shieldmaiden like chattel consider his fate.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.13** — Well, it sounds like you can fight, at least. Do you need employment?

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.13** — You soiled the sacred tradition of marriage! You soiled it with blood!

**str_npc_signup_2.13** — If you have a company-in-arms, and you vow to honor your word and your debts, I am willing to serve in it.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.13** — I have one, and I can do that.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.13** — Let me think about this a bit.

**str_npc_payment.13** — Very good. I would ask for {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} up front. I kill those who cheat me, and then afterwards it can be hard to collect payment.

**str_npc_intro.14** — Greetings - hello - if you don't mind ... - got a minute?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.14** — I might. What is it?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.14** — ...

**str_npc_backstory_a.14** — Look, I'm very sorry to trouble you, but - I notice you seem to be a wanderer. A fighter, like - a mercenary or something. I'd like to join you.

**str_npc_intro.15** — Know before you speak to me, that I am under a curse.

**str_npc_intro_response_1.15** — What sort of curse?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.15** — Heavens protect us from evil! Go away! Go away!

**str_npc_backstory_a.15** — When I was just a baby, a woman came to my father's hall, a woman who was said to be able to speak to the Otherworld. When she saw me, she told him that she saw the mark of the faeries upon me. She performed a divination, and said she had learned that I was to be a prank played on mankind: I should grow up to be a great beauty, but that any man who resolves to marry me shall die.

**str_npc_backstory_b.15** — Well, he did not believe in such things, so he laughed, tossed her a few coins, and sent her on her way. I grew up. When my first suitor was skewered by a spear in battle, I grieved, but thought little of it. When my second suitor passed of a fever, I was unnerved. When my third suitor was thrown from his horse on a hunt, I knew I must do something.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.15** — A tragic story, my lady. Please continue.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.15** — Faeries? I have no time for such tales.

**str_npc_backstory_d.15** — It is hard to find a lord who will take me in his retinue, as men tend to fear me. So opportunities for work are few and far between.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.15** — I'll take anyone, faerie-marked or not, if they can hold a place in a battle-line.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.15** — Mm... I agree with the lords who don't like to mess with the Otherworld.

**str_npc_signup_2.15** — Just be sure you tell your men of the curse upon me, as I would not wish to take anyone else's life, if it can be avoided.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.15** — Certainly. A very sensible precaution.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.15** — Oh... Hm... Look, warriors can be a bit credulous... Maybe we should give this a pass.

**str_npc_payment.15** — Good. I would merely ask from you an advance of {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}, to settle all affairs, and I shall join you.

**str_npc_intro.16** — Who are you? What do you want?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.16** — I merely meant to toast your health. As strangers sometimes do in taverns, without meaning any harm.

**str_npc_intro_response_2.16** — Never mind.

**str_npc_backstory_a.16** — Ah. I am sorry. It has been long since I spoke with other men. And I am a bit drunk... Look, let me tell you my story.

**str_npc_backstory_b.16** — I'm from the fen Dairl. We're not one of the biggest clans of Battania, but we're good fighters. When I came of age, I left my father's home for some years to live in the woods, as a Wolfskin. It is a custom we have, for youths to run as Wolfskins. They don't eat cooked food or live in houses or wear spun cloth, and in turn are not answerable to the laws of men.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.16** — I think I've heard of that custom. Don't the Battanians say it teaches them the ways of the woods?

**str_npc_interrupt_2.16** — I did not ask to hear your story. I have other business.

**str_npc_backstory_d.16** — I am sorry. It has been a long time since I spoke at such length to anyone. I think it is the wine. It has gone to my head. It has been three years that I have lived in the woods, with only the wolves for companions.

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.16** — Three years by yourself? You must have learned a great deal of woodcraft. I may have need of a scout.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.16** — ....

**str_npc_signup.16** — Patrols and hunting parties would sometimes come into the woods. I could run circles around them, and they would never know I was there.

**str_npc_signup_2.16** — [what he won't do]

**str_npc_signup_response_1.16** — Good. I can agree to that.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.16** — On second thought, you've been a while by yourself. Maybe you shouldn't join a company just yet.

**str_npc_payment.16** — Good. Can you.. Can you give me {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} in advance? I need better boots.

**str_npc_intro.17** — Hallo, stranger! Have a drink on me, for on a day such as today, it is not fitting for anyone to stand glum and sober in my presence!

**str_npc_intro_response_1.17** — Very well. What makes today such a special day?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.17** — I drink when I am thirsty, and not when some lout forces a cup into my hand.

**str_npc_backstory_a.17** — Why, just a few hours ago, I stole my hundredth horse! And such a horse it was. I saw it in the train of a caravan coming into the city. It was as though the Heavens said to the four winds: 'Come together and form sinews and bone, and make its coat a shining grey, and a white blaze upon its nose! Alas, it was an unworthy animal. It threw me and returned to his owner. But still, a day worth remembering, is it not?

**str_npc_backstory_b.17** — My father was a servant of the fen Uvain. By the age of 15, it was clear that as a trainer of horses, I had no equal. Melidir fen Uvain made me an offer. serve him for three years, and they'd give me the pick of the herd. At the end of the third year, when I was to claim my reward, Melidir's stablemaster told me that he'd just given every horse in his herd as a gift to his son. If I wanted, I could have a goat.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.17** — How droll of them...

**str_npc_interrupt_2.17** — ....

**str_npc_backstory_d.17** — Alas, I have had better luck taking horses than keeping them. And sooner or later, if I keep this up, I suppose I must end up in a noose. One hundred horses is a good enough point at which to quit, is it not? I must look for honest work. I don't suppose you have any such work to offer?

**str_npc_signup.17** — Far more than a horsethief, my good man. I am the prince of horsethieves! I have stolen Aserai mares from amid the tents and ridden them across the desert plans under the moon, I have taken Vlandian stallions from their paddocks, the sturdy ponies of the Khuzaits, and the steady geldings of the imperial lancers. Is there a bard in the house? Are you getting all this down, or shall I start again?

**str_npc_signup_2.17** — Also, as I told you, as of this afternoon I'm a reformed horsethief. You won't find a better judge of horses than me.

**str_npc_signup_response_1.17** — Well. A man who knows horses is always welcome. I pay each week, not after every three years.

**str_npc_signup_response_2.17** — ...

**str_npc_payment.17** — That's grand. That's most generous. But I hope you'll forgive me if, given the harsh lessons I've learned in the past, if I ask for a small advance - {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON}, if you don't mind.

**str_npc_payment_response.17** — That's reasonable. Here's {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} for you. Make yourself ready.

**str_npc_intro.18** — Hello, traveller. The wanderer is a blessing to the lands through which he passes.

**str_npc_intro_response_1.18** — That's kind of you to say.

**str_npc_intro_response_2.18** — I've met some who aren't, the ones who burn your village. Your type, from the look of you.

**str_npc_backstory_a.18** — It is a polite saying among my people, but it is also truth. The world would be a finer place if men could travel at will, bringing wisdom and wealth from one faraway place to another.

**str_npc_backstory_b.18** — When I was a child, I was taken from my home in the deep steppe as a hostage to the Empire, and though it was bitter to leave my family, I count that the luckiest thing that ever happened to me.

**str_npc_intro.19** — I see you, spirit! What have you come to tell me this time?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.19** — Hello? Hello? You look as though you are staring right through me.

**str_npc_intro_response_2.19** — You my hair on edge. Good day, sir.

**str_npc_backstory_a.19** — Wait! Silence! You'll frighten it! Ah... Never mind. It is gone.

**str_npc_backstory_b.19** — Pardon me for that. I see thing that others do not. Spirits of the Otherworld, who cross into our world for a brief flicker of time. I am sorry  - I know it is disturbing for those around me. But I must pay attention to them.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.19** — How fascinating. Do tell me more.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.19** — Talking with spirits, are we? I'll not interrupt your conversation.

**str_npc_backstory_c.19** — I began seeing them after my mother vanished. At first we thought that raiders had taken her, or wolves. That is life in the steppe, where we lived. But the spirits told me that my mother had not been taken, she had gone Below, to gather the spirits of other members of her family. I must be ready to conduct the ceremony for her return.

**str_npc_backstory_d.19** — Our own world and the Otherworld are shadows of each other, you see. Every time I see the spirits, they tell me to follow someone - a caravan, a raiding party, a group of mercenaries. I join that party, and it leads me to another. In this way I have crossed Calradia and crossed it again. Now they are telling me to follow you.

**str_npc_intro.20** — Greetings, stranger. Looking for someone to shed blood for you?

**str_npc_intro_response_1.20** — Um, I might be. Do you have some relevant experience?

**str_npc_intro_response_2.20** — Not at present, madame. Good day to you.

**str_npc_backstory_a.20** — Oh yes. I do indeed.

**str_npc_backstory_b.20** — I was born out on the steppe, but imperial slavers took me when I was a girl. The Empire had legends of warrior-women out in the deep steppe, and when I was sold, they claimed I was one of these - to entertain them by making their legends come true. They taught be to use a sword, and I learned well.

**str_npc_interrupt_1.20** — Yes. Go on.

**str_npc_interrupt_2.20** — This is fascinating, but I'm a bit pressed for time. Good-day for now.

**str_npc_backstory_c.20** — Well, perhaps there is something to those legends, because I did very well for myself, and made my master very rich. Imperial law now decrees that men are not allowed to kill in the arena, but no one pries into what happens at the private entertainments of the rich, and over a score of my fellow slaves must have felt my blade in their chest.

**str_npc_backstory_d.20** — Each kill won my master a chest of silver. I feel no guilt - my opponents were trying to kill me, and some came very close. Do you have anything to say to that?

**str_npc_backstory_response_1.20** — No, no. Do go on.

**str_npc_backstory_response_2.20** — I don't really have work like that, if that's what you're asking.

**str_npc_signup.20** — There's not much more to say. My master was a debauched animal but he let me keep a small share of my winnings, and eventually buy my freedom. I think he may also have realized that eventually, had he kept me against my will, he'd have ended up with a severed neck vein.

**str_npc_signup_2.20** — So here I am, looking to make a living through the only means I know - shedding other people's blood. Got work?

**str_npc_signup_response_1.20** — I'm not sure I can pay you like he did...

**str_npc_signup_response_2.20** — I'm not sure you're quite what I'm looking for...

**str_npc_payment.20** — I know what a hired blade makes, and I expect no more payment than anyone else in your company. But I would ask you for a small fee in advance to ensure you're not thinking of cheating me. Shall we say {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} denars?

**str_npc_payment_response.20** — I can afford to pay {NPCPAYMENT}{GOLD_ICON} denars. Make yourself ready.

## Wanderer (Companion) Strings
*Source: `SandBox/ModuleData/wanderer_strings.xml` — 537 entries*

**spc_prebackstory_generic** — (prebackstory generic remark for outside taverns)

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_0** — I don't mind talking about it.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_0** — I'm an engineer. Most of us learned our trade and got our contacts through the army. It was a good system: it was the emperor's money, so the emperor's servants kept a close eye on us. But as everyone knows, the emperor ran out of money. The lords are in charge of fortifications now, and all they have to go on is the say-so of other engineers.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_0** — You can imagine - it's a bit of a racket. People build arches that fall down, and his colleagues go on recommending him because he's someone's brother or old apprentice. The greatest sin in our brotherhood is criticizing the work of other engineers.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_0** — Well, I don't play that game. If something's going to fall down and kill someone, I'll point that out. So, naturally, all my 'brothers' cut me out of contracts.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_0** — Most noble of you, sir.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_0** — A man of integrity, or simply one who backbites his peers? I have no idea, and wouldn't want to take the risk of hiring you.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_0** — So, anyway, I am forced to spend my time in taverns, taking whatever work can be found. I can oversee the building of most structures, or, if the need is there, I am also adept at knocking them down with catapults, rams, and mines.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_0** — I'm an engineer, with imperial army training. I'm sure by now you've met a few of us around, and know a bit about what we can do.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_1** — You want to know about me? Well, that's a story, that's a story.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_1** — See, there's a lot of tales about me, and only some of them are true. The Khuzaits call me by one name, the Aserai by another.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_1** — I've been in a lot of fights and I've killed a lot of people. Ask you around - you shouldn't just take my word for it. But never one who didn't deserve it, and never once outside a fair fight.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_1** — Let me tell you something else - war is not a game. It's not a game. Play by the rules and you die. The streets aren't the arena. If you think someone's your enemy, you take them down - don't wait for a polite challenge.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_1** — Ah, yes. Wise words. Do go on.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_1** — You've said nothing about yourself, and your one word contradicts the other. I have better things to do.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_1** — I don't like to brag about my own deeds, so I'll leave it at that. I do a lot of work for the merchants around here, but they don't own me. I'm my own man. I just take their money. It's not like I'm a mercenary or something like that.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_1** — I'm a warrior. A soldier of fortune, you might say. A damn good one, too, as my enemies would tell you if they could speak from the other world.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_2** — It is not without some reluctance that I tell this story, for it hardly does honor to my name.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_2** — My father was a cataphract in the east. We had a small estate to pay for his horse and armor. I was raised to take his place on the imperial troop rosters when he came of age.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_2** — But the Khuzaits overran us, and he was slain, and our land was taken. Its revenues now belong to some tarkhan. Alas, the empire has little land to grant today, even to trained cavalrymen like myself who wish to serve. And horses are expensive.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_2** — You may call it pride, but I do not wish to enlist as a foot soldier. So I work here in town, for merchants, for pay, a hired sword. All I can say is that I hope one day to purchase the land I need to serve our emperor, whoever sits in the throne, as my father did.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_2** — That's it? The dishonorable part? That you work for merchants? I'd thought it would be a lot worse.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_2** — A cavalier of the empire doing errands for traders! The shame of it!

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_2** — I try at least to pick and choose my master, and hope at least that some of our equestrian honor rubs off on the men of commerce.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_2** — I'm a former imperial cataphract. Our skills, and our honor, needs no further introduction. But I was unable to afford my horse and armor, so I took work with merchants, as a hired sword.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_3** — Refill my glass and I'll tell you.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_3** — I'm a soldier by trade. I've served in the empire's legions for 20 years. Once upon a time they were worthy of being called 'legions.' We served together for years, and we'd die rather than see our standards falter or fall.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_3** — But Drosios Neretzes led the pick of the legions into an ambush in the Battanian woods. You may have heard that story. I was laid up sick at the time. But a lot of my comrades didn't come back, and things were never the same afterward.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_3** — After Arenicos's so-called reforms, they try to maintain an army on the cheap, letting the rich run the show out of their own pocket. No wonder the whole thing's collapsed into a bunch of squabbling factions and we're mocked by the barbarians we used to rule.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_3** — No doubt a sad state of affairs. So what do you do?

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_3** — Ah, the old days. And no doubt back then they complained about the older days. I've heard enough.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_3** — Well, I can't just sit around and drink myself to death, so I sell my sword to anyone worth following. I'm a good trainer - I don't bother with horsemen or archers, but if you've got good steady footmen I can do a lot with them. I know a bit about siege machinery too.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_3** — I'm a soldier of the imperial legions. How we came to this sorry state is a sad tale that you've no doubt heard already from my comrades. But I'm sure you're familiar with our mettle in battle, and our skill at turning youths into soldiers.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_4** — Oh, I suppose I can tell you. Nothing that no one doesn't already know, no how.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_4** — Me and some lads from my village, we thought we'd run away, join some other lads up there who make their living on the highways, if you know what I mean. Didn't much want to go scratching a plow across the dry fields all year every year like my father did.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_4** — But I was young and foolish. Bandits - well, who'd have thought? They're real animals. Always drunk and stabbing each other, or too drunk to feel cold so they catch the plague and end up coughing up blood, or drunk and asleep when the patrol comes around so they end up on the gallows - I suspect you get the idea.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_4** — So that was no kind of life, neither. I left the woods, paid a little money to friends who got my name off the outlaw list, and now I'm a regular law-abiding citizen. Officially, that is.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_4** — A wise decision.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_4** — A knave who could not abide other men's knavery! May such wonders never cease.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_4** — Life's better here in the city. More 'civilized,' you could say. Oh, the work can be a bit rough and tumble, but I feel I can relax after a long day with more refined company, like your good self.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_4** — When I was a lad, I dabbled in crime and banditry a bit, but am now seeking more honest work. I still like the fighting and killing part, though. Anyway, I'm sure you've met a fair amount of men like me on your journeys.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_5** — You're a nosy one, I see.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_5** — What do you want to know about? My family? Piss on them. I left home as a child and never had cause to regret it. My brothers can take my inheritance, and I hope they choke on it.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_5** — I've fought in a few wars, for one side or the other. You want to know about my-comrades-in-arms? Piss on them too. They all turn on you in the end.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_5** — About my past, that's all I have to say.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_5** — So... What are you good at?

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_5** — You're a cheerful one. Good day to you.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_5** — I can fight. And I don't mind doing work that others would shirk.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_5** — I kill for a living. You don't look too wet behind the ears, so I'm sure I don't need to tell you any more about myself than that.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_6** — I'll tell you my story.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_6** — You may have heard of Ladimos the Red. He preached that the Heavens were getting ready to unload their wrath on landowners and merchant, that we had to drive them out and live pure lives and we'd be rewarded with a Pure Emperor, come down from the skies. This was some 10 years ago. Well, a lot of us ran off to follow him, some of us believed him and some of us had debts and some just wanted to take a lick at those that oppressed us.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_6** — We built a great temple in the back country, out in the bush, called it the Kingdom of Truth. We whipped two imperial detachments sent to track us down. But Ladimos died, 'Called up to Heaven' he said on his deathbed, and then we lost our way a bit. We needed food and we needed money, so our chiefs started collecting 'taxes' from the villages below. Some started taking money from lords and merchants for protection of caravans. And those who grumbled - well, they started turning up dead in the dry streambeds.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_6** — So I left. And a short while later the emperor sent a third detachment, bigger than the others, and that was the end of the Kingdom of Truth. My old comrades - I see them sometimes from time to time, some in a lord's retinue, others in a cage with R for 'robber' branded on their forehead.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_6** — A sad tale.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_6** — Heresy, rebellion, and looting are three intertwined serpents. You should bear that brand yourself, knave.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_6** — I learned a few skills up in the hills, how to follow a trail and spot an ambush, most useful to caravaneers. So I reckon I can probably stay ahead of the hangman. A regular job wouldn't hurt, though.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_6** — Aye, well, once I was a rebel up in the back country, but rebels never last too long. Now I just want to serve and get paid. You've been around. You've met men like me before, I'm sure.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_7** — Yeah, I'll tell you my story. Pass the wine and listen close.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_7** — My family had debts, so I signed up to be a soldier under one of Old Neretzes's kinsmen. I guess I always liked men's work more than women's work. The legions took hill women as scouts but I was never the hidey-sneaky type. So I did what I did to be in the spear line.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_7** — Dressed as a man, of course. Weren't difficult to do. Not hard to fool men. Bound my breasts and watched where I pissed. It was easy.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_7** — Then one day our commander led us into an ambush. The apple doesn't far fall from the tree, you could say. I didn't see the battle but was part of the rout. That was the end of army life for me. Don't care for glory-hounding lords leading me to my death. But I still like to fight.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_7** — Well, there's always work for the brave and the resourceful.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_7** — A rather sad tale of deceit and disgrace.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_7** — Yeah.. The merchants give me jobs. But I'm not sure I care much for guarding caravans. A lot of sitting around listening to boring talk about prices. Look, I can wield a sword or spear and I can also repair them. Wouldn't mind trying my hand them at making them too. If you've know a captain with a good company, a fighting company, maybe he'd be interested.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_7** — I dressed as a man to serve in the legions. There are many of us who've done that, believe it or not. You've probably met one of us before, even if you didn't know it.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_8** — I'll tell you my story. If it bothers you, I'd prefer you keep it to yourself - unless you've lived months on crusts of bread and chaff of grain, that is.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_8** — My father was a merchant in {IMPERIALCAPITAL}. We lived in a rich house, with many servants. I wanted for nothing. Our neighbor was a moneylender, who specialized in loans to the imperial guard. That turned out to be a bad neighborhood in which to live, when the riots came.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_8** — The guardsmen came to burn our neighbor's house, so their debts would be forgotten. The flames spread to our house, and it was destroyed. My father tried to save his strongbox, and that was his undoing. A riot is a holiday for thieves and robbers, and some saw him dragging it through the streets, so they knifed him and took it. We tried to find shelter with my uncle, but there was no food in the city, and he turned us out. So we joined the refugees in the country, living on what we could steal from the fields.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_8** — I found a guardsman, alone and drunk. I have no idea whether he was one of the ones that set fire to our neighborhood. Maybe I should not have done to him what I did to him. But now I have his sword. It's been very useful.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_8** — The starving do what they must.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_8** — And to think you had all the advantages of an educated childhood.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_8** — I think my story shows that I am adaptable, at least. If there was room for me in a warlord's retinue, say, I imagine I could quickly learn whatever skills were needed.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_8** — I was a merchant's daughter. There was a bout of unrest in our home city, and our home and warehouses were burned and our family made penniless. I shall spare you the details. I am sure you've heard plenty of similar tales in these times.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_9** — Aye, so you want my story then?

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_9** — Far back as I remember, I was living on the streets of {IMPERIALCAPITAL} with a bunch of other dirty, barefoot scrogs. A group of men in our alley, they called themselves the Centaurs, I guess they took a liking to me. Gave me special errands to run from them - started with picking pockets, ended with sticking knives into their enemies. Back then I'd do anything for a handful of figs and cheese and a pat on the head.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_9** — Got a bit older though, and their interest in me changed. Filthy drunken louts pressing themselves against me, grabbing at me - I wasn't having that. Made up my mind to leave, but wasn't sure where to go.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_9** — Then came the day that {IMPERIALCAPITAL} burned, and everyone was out looting and robbing, and that was my chance. Lifted a bag of silver from the Centaurs' stash and lit out on the road.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_9** — A hard life, but I must admire your fortitude, at least.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_9** — You truly are the dregs of the street, my lady.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_9** — Anyway, I wandered about a bit, but now I think it's time I found steady work. You wouldn't need someone to stick a knife in those that need sticking, do you?

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_9** — I was an orphan, you see. Worked for a gang, as our kind must so often do. Did their foul work for them. But they perished in a siege, and I decided to strike out on my own, see what this fine land of Calradia could offer me.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_10** — I can tell you my story, though it is painful to recall.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_10** — I'm a surgeon. I trained at the imperial academy in {IMPERIALCAPITAL}. I had many rich and influential patients in the town. I thought I was well shielded from the intrigues and dangers of the Empire.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_10** — But one day I was contacted by an agent of the Bureau of Barbarian Affairs. I do not know how well you know them. Their original mission was to keep the foreign tribes divided and weak, but they expanded their remit into all the affairs of the empire, anything that might be deemed a threat. At first they wanted small harmless details about my patients. To do so was a violation of my oath, but I was anxious to have the favor of the Bureau. But soon they began to call on me for more and more.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_10** — One time they came at midnight - they had a man who plotted against the Emperor, they said, and they needed a confession, and wished me to use my art to elicit that confession. If I refused, they said, they would disclose our relationship to my patients - I would be ruined. I went with them, to my shame, and what I was asked to do to that man's body -- I shall not repeat it.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_10** — You too are a victim of the hideous power of the state.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_10** — You broke your oath. It is not surprising that you fell further.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_10** — I should have refused - my practice was ruined anyway. To blot out the memory of that night, I took opium, until my pallid face so alarmed my patients that they no longer called on me. So I fled the city, and have wandered from town to town ever since. I would welcome steady work, if I could find it.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_10** — I was a surgeon, trained at the imperial academy. But my home and infirmary were burned in a bout of unrest, and now I must wander the world a bit. There are many of us out there, you know, forced to make what living we can.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_11** — Yes... I can tell you my tale...

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_11** — My father was an imperial cataphract. Alas, he died in battle against the Aserai, and I was placed under the local archon's guardianship. He had eyes for my father's estate, modest as it was, so he arranged for me to be married to his cousin.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_11** — But this cousin... I would not marry that man! He was a boor, a drunk - never there was a night that he did not reek of wine, never a morning that he did not reek of vomit! But a cataphract's daughter is not some chit you can marry against her will. I took a horse from my father's estate - my horse, legally - his old sword, and rode off.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_11** — So, here I am. Perhaps I am not the most experienced of warriors, but I can learn. I cannot go back - I learned that the archon filed suit that I stole a horse - my own horse, by right! - which shows you what a cad he is.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_11** — You've got spirit, I'll give you that.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_11** — Takes more to being a warrior than a horse and a sword, young one.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_11** — So, here I am, looking for a captain under whom to serve. I know the ways of an archon's court, and I know how to ride, but I am looking to master the ways of the sword. And if I learn my trade well, perhaps I shall one day reclaim my birthright!

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_11** — I fled a bad marriage. There are many like me; I meet them in every tavern in Calradia. I am lucky in that my father was a cataphract, and taught me to ride and fight before he died, and I suppose that's how I must make a living.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_0** — You know, we women suffer greatly when you warriors have your sport...

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_0** — I lived in a village to the north of here, across the gulf. It is a cruel land; there is no strong king, and lords think nothing of ravaging their neighbor's lands. My mother was skilled in the use of herbs to treat disease and wounds. I had a happy peaceful childhood - until one day, a month before I was to be married.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_0** — That was the day my life changed. A band from a nearby village came and attacked us. We had done them no harm; we had never even thought of them as our enemies. But they wanted our cattle. They killed my mother and the youth who I was to marry, and burned our village. Everything gone. Those who lived fled into the woods.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_0** — I expect that my kin will soon return to their homes, but I will not.  I cannot... I cannot be in a place where I am at the mercy of any beast on the rampage. I will ply my trade among warriors. I will learn to harm as well as to heal. And if the time comes for me to marry, I will live in a land where there is a king, even a tyrant, rather than raising a family amid the war of all against all.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_0** — I am sorry for your fate, my lady.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_0** — It's a cruel world, and if you think a warrior's life is any easier, you have a painful lesson in store.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_0** — At any rate, if you know of a warband who is looking for someone who knows how to treat wounds, I would be grateful.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_0** — I was an herbalist in a village in the north. But our home was raided, and I've been forced to wander in search of work. There are many like me on the roads of Calradia.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_1** — Yes.. My story... Jealousy, envy of my talents. That's always been my undoing.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_1** — When I was a boy, I was the best fighter in my village. 'You're stronger as a boy than a full-grown warrior,' people would say. I'm not boasting here - that's what they'd tell me. So when I came of age I went off to make my fortune.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_1** — Started in the Vaegir guard. I found that I was the only real warrior among them. They were all about marching here and there in their pretty uniforms, not pulling sword from scabbard for months on end. I told them what I thought, and my captain told me to keep my mouth shut or leave. So I left.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_1** — Then I joined the Skolderbroda. The 'Shield Brothers.' It's a good name, you know? They spent most of their time hunkering behind their shields. Ha! Me, I'd wade into the midst of the enemy, dealing out death right and left - and, well, all they had to say afterward was 'Why didn't you keep ranks?'

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_1** — Hmm... Strange response.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_1** — Has no one told you that leaving a gap in a shield wall is as good as treason?

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_1** — So I'm having no more of that. I'm on the look-out for an outfit that employs real fighters.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_1** — Let me tell you friend, I'm hard. I've fought with the Skolderbroda, the Vaegirs, any mercenaries worth their salt, I've been with them. Others may tell you've they've done what I've done, but I'm the real thing.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_2** — Certainly - I make no secret of my ambitions.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_2** — My father was one of the leading warriors of our clan, but in his last battle his hamstring was cut. We've lived well off the wealth he brought home from his raids, buying land and thralls, but now I feel it's time that I bring home some silver of my own.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_2** — I need to buy a ship, and hire men to row it. But I do not wish to sell our land to outfit a risky voyage, to risk depriving my father and mother of their comforts in old age, and my brothers of their hopes for a good marriage.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_2** — So I have resolved to hire out my sword and make enough money for such a ship. Having done so, I shall take it to faraway shores and bring home silver and slaves so that we may buy land enough for all. In this way I will do my duty to my family.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_2** — You are a most dutiful son and brother.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_2** — Such pieties from a man who intends to pillage the labor of others.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_2** — At any rate, if you know the leader of warband who's generous and honorable, he'll find no braver warrior to follow him than me.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_2** — My father sent me off into the world, to build our fortune with my sword. This is a common story among the sons of our people.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_3** — Aye - you've heard about the death of the last Emperor?

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_3** — I'll tell you - what most people believe is a pack of lies. I was in the Vaegir guard in the time of Arenicos. We took our discipline seriously; we were proud of it. Then the riots happened. What I saw in {IMPERIALCAPITAL}.. Even now it makes me feel ashamed.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_3** — It wasn't easy for the men. They felt the city turn against them, blame them for killing the emperor. Whereas we were sure that we were innocent of his blood, that there was some sort of trick. But even so, there was no excuse.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_3** — We could have marched out in battle array. No one would have stood against us. If we couldn't restore order, at least we could have gone home with honor. But instead, we turned our anger against the city. My comrades looted, set fires, even murdered those who we were supposed to protect. It was a disgrace.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_3** — I have heard about the riots in {IMPERIALCAPITAL}. It was an ugly thing all round.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_3** — The Guard didn't kill the Emperor? Funny, that's not what the witnesses said.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_3** — I thought of going home. But I lost what denars I had saved during the riots. If there is a warband looking for good men, I would like to earn it back.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_3** — I was part of the old Emperor Arenicos's Vaegir Guard. But the people turned on us after his death, and attacked us. Maybe you've heard the story before. There's a whole lot of us, spat out into the world by the ungrateful Calradians.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_4** — It's not many who ask that question.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_4** — I was a farmer. But I split a man's head open with a hoe. He was also a farmer. It was a dispute over a broken fence, between my pasture and his. I had no intention of killing him.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_4** — His cousins came for me, to take me to judgment. I would have gone willingly; I would have paid blood-money. Gladly. But one of them laid hands on me, and a black rage came over me, and I killed two of them, too. I didn't want to kill them either.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_4** — That was that. I could pay blood money for one man but not three. I fled. I cannot return.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_4** — It sounds like you had no choice.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_4** — A man who cannot master his rage is a greater threat then the man who murders with intent.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_4** — If the choice I had been mine, I would have never hurt anyone. I would live on my land, eat what I had grown, marry and have children. But the Heavens have decreed that I should eat by shedding other men's blood. In the city, rich men pay me well for that.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_4** — I was a farmer once. I killed a man in a fight and could not pay the blood money, so I had to flee. It's a common enough tale in the northlands. I accept that my destiny will be blood and hardship, rather than the simple life on the land I once craved.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_5** — Look, friend, I'm here to drink, not talk. But if you really want to know, I'll give it to you in brief.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_5** — We Sturgians have a tradition. If two people have a dispute, and there's no witnesses, so it all comes down to one man's word against another's, then we let them settle it with swords. If one man doesn't like to fight, he can hire someone else to do the fighting. That's how it works with us. Probably other people do the same, because it's a good tradition.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_5** — I like to fight, so I made it known that I'd fight for anyone if the price is right. Shed a little blood, make a little coin, drink it away, make a little more, all in the cause of justice. Not a bad life, eh?

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_5** — Well, I guess I showed myself a bit too eager. The councils stopped accepting me as champion. Told me I sold my sword too cheaply, they said. What can I say? I have to look for other work now. It's a damn shame. I like duels - you don't worry about arrows, or someone coming up from behind. No need to stay sober for hours on end waiting for a fight that never comes. Just a few minutes of trouble, a bit of blood, and then usually a good meal afterwards.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_5** — Councils these days. Always making changes...

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_5** — You call that the cause of justice?

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_5** — But look - I'd still be a fine addition to a fighting company. I know how to swing a sword and an axe, and know a thing or two about forging them and keeping them sharp as well.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_5** — I was a sword for hire. Specialized in duels - you know, when there's a trial, and you can't work it out any other way. But you can run that racket too long - eventually the councils start banning you from fighting - so now here I am.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_6** — I'll tell you, but I don't know why you'd be interested.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_6** — My parents died when I was young. My sister married. Her husband wanted my parents' farm. So he hired a devious man, a fast-talker, who knew the law well. He said... I don't even remember what he said, in court, before the council. But the council awarded both of them the farm.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_6** — It did not matter much. I always preferred the woods. I made a better living shooting squirrels and rabbits and selling fur.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_6** — But I've been thinking.. Maybe I want to marry. And I guess I need more silver for that, probably more than I can get from the squirrels. So... People tell me that warleaders will pay for a good scout. And I know the woods well.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_6** — That seems a reasonable ambition. A good scout can command a high price.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_6** — What woman wouldn't relish a husband smelling of half-cured skins, slept in for the whole winter?

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_6** — I know the woods well. I can move quickly in them. I'll tell you all about a war party from the branches it broke marching through.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_6** — I'm a trapper, a hunter. Used to be I could make a good living through furs... But with all these bandits about.... I'd rather be part of an army, I think. Spent my whole life in the woods and I reckon I could do well as a scout.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_7** — I'll tell you my story. Why not?

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_7** — My father was a draftsman. He helped build towers and walls for the boyars. I used to help him in his work, drawing up his plans. I had a good hand for that. We went from town to town, employer to employer, just the two of us. It was a wonderful time, until he dropped dead, just before I entered my twelfth year.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_7** — My mother had already died, so I was taken in by my uncle. But he didn't really want me. See, I had a birthmark on my shoulder, the kind that some people means the bearer can cast the Evil Eye. Whenever there was sickness in the streets of my uncles' village, the people would mutter and curse at me. Eventually they demanded my uncle drive me out of the village. It was no great loss for him to comply. Probably saved him worry over where he was going to find the money to marry me off.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_7** — I wandered from village to village, begging and stealing. You may imagine how I fared at the mercy of the robbers of the road, who had no more fear of sorcery then they did of man's laws. But eventually I learned to protect myself, and the body of one careless bandit afforded me with my first sword and leather jerkin.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_7** — A sad tale. Please continue.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_7** — Heavens protect us from evil! Away! Away!

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_7** — That is all there is to say, really. I still have the sword, and it is for hire, to those who pay well. I still remember a bit of my father's trade, too. I'll do most whatever is needed. The world had no mercy on me, so I feel no need to show any.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_7** — I don't know where I came from. First thing I remember is wandering the roads with a bunch of other orphans, going from village to village begging and stealing. But now, you see, I've stolen a sword from a group of bandits we found sleeping off a drunken night, and I figure maybe I can be something different.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_8** — I'll tell you my tale. But I will warn you in advance: It is of no concern to me whether you approve or disapprove of what I did.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_8** — I came from a good family, with much land. Since I was a girl, I wished to be a shield-maiden. I practiced fighting with the village boys and the old warriors. But it is a strange thing - while some families in our lands take pride in a daughter who takes up arms, others accord it a great shame, and my father was of the latter type.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_8** — I had no special desire to be married but my family found me a groom anyway. I consented, but my husband and I detested each other from the first. Once he insulted me in the marketplace, I cursed his manhood, he struck me, and I pulled a knife and he pulled his. I won.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_8** — The elders sat in judgment on our case. As it turned out, they had plenty of precedent. They accorded our fight a fair duel, and thus I was innocent of murder. On the other hand, I was excluded from his inheritance. I suppose that was fair, although I would have enjoyed wearing his jewels and riding his horse in front of his family.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_8** — Indeed. No doubt such traditions encourages husbands to behave better than they might do otherwise.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_8** — You slew your husband in a duel? Get away!

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_8** — Suffice to say, I could not return to my father's house. I went on my way, happy to live the life of a warrior I had always dreamed of living. But soon I found out - the tales I loved as a girl, of shield-maidens who fought for honor, do not pertain to a woman with no family or land. One cannot fight for honor when one doesn't know where the next meal comes from. So I fight for pay.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_8** — I am a warrior. A shield-maiden, as the Nords say. It is not uncommon in the northern lands. Perhaps you have met some of us before.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_9** — Pour yourself a drink stranger. I'll tell you all you need to know.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_sturgia_9** — How would I put it? I guess I'd say I'm a lady who's gotten a reputation for doing a man's work better then the men. I guess I'm a bit of a rarity. Although that's a bit of a surprise to me.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_sturgia_9** — You won't find me passed out in the straw in my own vomit when needed for a task. You won't have to bribe the guard to get me out of a cell because I got on a fight on my way to work.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_sturgia_9** — Instead, for my fee, I'll make sure that those who need protecting are protected, and those who need to die are dead.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_sturgia_9** — Yes... So hard to find a dependable fighter these days.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_sturgia_9** — I don't begrudge a warrior a few drinks and a fight from time to time.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_sturgia_9** — Anyway, you come across a chief who needs a reliable sword in his warband, you let me know.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_sturgia_9** — I guess I'd say that I'm just a lady who didn't care for her distaff, and took up a spear instead. If you want to know more, hire me, point me at your enemies, and I'll show you rather than tell you.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_battania_0** — Certainly. The more who know about my skills, the better.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_battania_0** — The women in our family passed down the art of healing from generation to generation, and other... em... services, that can be accomplished with herbs. But for all our skill we remained poor, while richly robed, well-fed men with half our skill walked about the towns tending to the lords and ladies.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_battania_0** — By the time I became a woman I was sick of filthy huts and puking babies. I came to the towns and inquired after which households, among those who had wealth, might have a patient for me. Of course when I showed up at the door in my torn, stained dress they slammed it in my face.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_battania_0** — So I acquired some denars - I will not say how - and with it bought a silk robe and some jewelry. This got me inside the doors of rich men's houses, and the cures I worked, and the reputation I earned, have done the rest.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_battania_0** — Sounds like you have a good head for business.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_battania_0** — Yes - many is the healer who has come to specialize in the diseases of the rich.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_battania_0** — But I've noticed something - more denars is spent on war than on anything else. So, if someone's raised an army, and doesn't want to lose their investment to infected wounds and fevers, well, it might be worthwhile to employ me.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_battania_0** — Once I was just another back-country healer, attending to squalling babies and superstitious villagers. But now I'm trying to make the money that my skill with medicine deserves.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_battania_1** — Pull up a chair, friend - you'll be glad you asked!

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_battania_1** — I could tell you of all my deeds, and you'd never believe me. But you know, if you'd met me a year back, I could have taken you to my hall some time and shown you them. Shown you my deeds! You heard that!

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_battania_1** — I do things in the old way, and so whenever an enemy falls to my spear, I take their head!
