**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EnterVillageTutorial** — Entering Settlements

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EnterVillageTutorial** — You have arrived at {TUTORIAL_SETTLEMENT_NAME}. To explore the location, you can enter the settlement by pressing the highlighted button on the left.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.NavigateOnMapTutorialStep1** — Navigating Calradia

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.NavigateOnMapTutorialStep1** — Welcome to Calradia!{newline}{newline}You can explore the world map by moving the camera with {FORWARD_KEY}{BACKWARDS_KEY}{LEFT_KEY}{RIGHT_KEY}, panning your view by right clicking and dragging your mouse and zooming in and out with the mouse wheel.{newline}{newline}Give it a try.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.NavigateOnMapTutorialStep1_controller** — Welcome to Calradia!{newline}{newline}You can explore the world map by moving the camera with {CONSOLE_MOVEMENT_KEY}, panning your view with {CONSOLE_CAMERA_KEY} and zooming in and out with {MAP_ZOOM_OUT_KEY} and {MAP_ZOOM_IN_KEY}.{newline}{newline}Give it a try.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.NavigateOnMapTutorialStep2** — Navigating Calradia

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.NavigateOnMapTutorialStep2** — Moving your party is done by clicking on the map. This will leave a mark on the target location - unless you have clicked on inaccessible areas such as mountains or sea.{newline}{newline}Let's set off to {TUTORIAL_SETTLEMENT_NAME}!

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.NavigateOnMapTutorialStep2_controller** — Moving your party is done by hovering the indicator on the map and pressing {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY}. This will leave a mark on the target location - unless you have hovered over an inaccessible areas such as mountains or sea.{newline}{newline}Let's set off to {TUTORIAL_SETTLEMENT_NAME}!

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.SeeMarkersInMissionTutorial** — Speak to the Headman

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.SeeMarkersInMissionTutorial** — You can hold {MISSION_INDICATORS_KEY} to see the location of the Headman.{newline}{newline}Once you are near him, press {INTERACTION_KEY} to speak with him.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.GetSuppliesTutorialStep1** — Buying Food

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GetSuppliesTutorialStep1** — You should purchase supplies from the settlement menu on the left.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.GetSuppliesTutorialStep2** — Buying Food

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GetSuppliesTutorialStep2** — You can filter Items through buttons at the top. Filter them to Misc.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.GetSuppliesTutorialStep3** — Buying Food

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GetSuppliesTutorialStep3** — Your brother recommends that you purchase 2 sacks of grain.{newline}{newline}You can do this by transferring them to your inventory with the little arrow on the left side

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.PressLeaveToReturnFromMissionType1** — Leaving a Mission

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.PressLeaveToReturnFromMissionType1** — To leave a mission, you can hold down {LEAVE_MISSION_KEY}.{newline}{newline}This will return you to the settlement menu where you can purchase supplies and hire recruits.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.PressLeaveToReturnFromMissionType2** — Leaving a Mission

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.PressLeaveToReturnFromMissionType2** — To leave a mission, you can hold down {LEAVE_MISSION_KEY}.{newline}{newline}This will return you to the settlement menu where you can purchase supplies and hire recruits.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.GetQuestTutorial** — Quests

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GetQuestTutorial** — You have an active quest! You can learn more about it by clicking on the quest log on the lower left of your screen.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GetQuestTutorial_controller** — You have an active quest! You can learn more about it by pressing {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the quest log on the lower left of your screen.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.TakeAndRescuePrisonerTutorial** — Rescuing & Taking Prisoners

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.TakeAndRescuePrisonerTutorial** — After a hard-fought battle, you may have the choice to take some prisoners or recruit those that you have freed from your enemy.{newline}{newline}Both options are done by transferring the troops to your party with the little arrow button on the left.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.StealthCrouchTutorial** — Crouching

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.StealthCrouchTutorial** — You are quieter and less visible when crouching. Try it now by pressing {CROUCH_KEY} and pass by the guard.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.StealthWalkSlowTutorial** — Walk Slow

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.StealthWalkSlowTutorial** — Press {WALK_MODE_KEY} to move slowly and reduce noise, making enemies less suspicious.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.StealthWalkSlowTutorial_controller** — Hold {CROUCH_KEY} and press {INTERACTION_KEY} to move slowly and reduce noise, making enemies less suspicious.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.StealthHideInBushesTutorial** — Tall Grass

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.StealthHideInBushesTutorial** — There is tall grass on the right of this passage. Use it to avoid the patrol.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.StealthDistractionTutorial** — Distraction

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.StealthDistractionTutorial** — You can distract guards with noise. Try throwing one of the stones in your inventory to grab their attention.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.StealthDarkZoneTutorial** — Darkness

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.StealthDarkZoneTutorial** — You are less visible in dark areas.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.StealthStealthKillTutorial** — Stealth Kill

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.StealthStealthKillTutorial** — You will deal additional damage when you hit an unaware enemy. Take out the remaining guard from behind.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.StealthHideCorpseTutorial** — Hide the Body

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.StealthHideCorpseTutorial** — If an enemy comes across a corpse, they will start investigating. You can avoid this by pressing {INTERACTION_KEY} to interact with the body to move it out of the way.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.RecruitmentTutorialStep1** — Recruitment

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.RecruitmentTutorialStep1** — Your brother has asked you to hire at least 4 men before you set out to face the raiders.{newline}{newline}You can hire troops from villages and towns by clicking on the "Recruit Troops" button.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.RecruitmentTutorialStep1_controller** — Your brother has asked you to hire at least 4 men before you set out to face the raiders.{newline}{newline}You can hire troops from villages and towns by pressing {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the "Recruit Troops" button.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.RecruitmentTutorialStep2** — Recruitment

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.RecruitmentTutorialStep2** — Notables help you recruit more and better (higher level) troops according to your relation with them.{newline}{newline}Click on some troops to move them into your party.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.RecruitmentTutorialStep2_controller** — Notables help you recruit more and better (higher level) troops according to your relation with them.{newline}{newline}Move troops into your party by pressing {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on their portraits.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.TalkToNotableTutorialStep1** — Talk to the headman

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.TalkToNotableTutorialStep1** — The menu on the top right shows the important people in your current location.{newline}{newline}Click on the headman's portrait to talk to him.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.TalkToNotableTutorialStep1_controller** — The menu on the top right shows the important people in your current location.{newline}{newline}Press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the headman's portrait to talk to him.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.TalkToNotableTutorialStep2** — Talk to the headman

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.TalkToNotableTutorialStep2** — Click on the "Visit" button to return to the notable and learn more about the task ahead.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.TalkToNotableTutorialStep2_controller** — Return to the notable and learn more about the task ahead by pressing {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the "Visit" button.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.OrderTutorial1TutorialStep1** — Battle Commands

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderTutorial1TutorialStep1** — At the beginning of a battle your soldiers will be holding their position. You can tell them to charge by opening the movement orders with {FIRST_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} and choosing "Follow Me" with {SECOND_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderTutorial1TutorialStep1_controller** — At the beginning of a battle your soldiers will be holding their position. You can tell them to follow by opening the order menu with {HOLD_OPEN_ORDER_KEY} and movement orders with {FIRST_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} and choosing "Follow Me" with {SECOND_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.OrderTutorial1TutorialStep2** — Battle Commands

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderTutorial1TutorialStep2** — You can tell your men to charge by opening the movement orders with {FIRST_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} and choosing charge with {THIRD_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderTutorial1TutorialStep2_controller** — You can tell your men to charge by opening the order menu with {HOLD_OPEN_ORDER_KEY} and movement orders with {FIRST_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} and choosing "Charge" with {THIRD_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.OrderTutorial2Tutorial** — Hideouts & Orders

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderTutorial2Tutorial** — Hideout missions begin with the enemy unaware of your approach.{newline}{newline}Order your troops to follow you with the {FIRST_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} and {SECOND_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} shortcuts and try to take them on in small groups.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderTutorial2Tutorial_controller** — Hideout missions begin with the enemy unaware of your approach.{newline}{newline}Open the order menu with {HOLD_OPEN_ORDER_KEY} and order your troops to follow you with the {FIRST_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} and {SECOND_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} shortcuts and try to take them on in small groups.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.MovementInMissionTutorial** — Movement

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.MovementInMissionTutorial** — You can move your character:{newline}- Forwards with {FORWARD_KEY}{newline}- Backwards with {BACKWARDS_KEY}{newline}- Left with {LEFT_KEY}{newline}- Right with {RIGHT_KEY}{newline}{newline}Try them all now!

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.MovementInMissionTutorial_controller** — You can move your character with {CONSOLE_MOVEMENT_KEY}.{newline}{newline}Try moving in four direction now!

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.UpgradingTroopsStep1** — Upgrading Troops

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.UpgradingTroopsStep1** — Some of your troops now have enough experience for an upgrade.{newline}{newline}To review and upgrade your troops click on the highlighted party screen button.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.UpgradingTroopsStep1_controller** — Some of your troops now have enough experience for an upgrade.{newline}{newline}To review and upgrade your troops press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the highlighted party screen button.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.UpgradingTroopsStep2** — Upgrading Troops

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.UpgradingTroopsStep2** — Troops that are ready to upgrade are marked with a special icon{UPGRADE_ICON}.{newline}{newline}The total number of upgradeable troops is shown inside the highlighted button, at the top right corner of the screen.{newline}{newline}Open the popup to upgrade some of your troops.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.UpgradingTroopsStep3** — Upgrading Troops

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.UpgradingTroopsStep3** — Troop upgrades will cost you denars and troop experience. Some troops may have two possible upgrade paths and may require items such as horses.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.BuyingFood** — Buying Foods

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.BuyingFoodStep1** — You must maintain food supplies at all times. If you run out of food, your party will lose morale. Your troops may desert you because of low morale.{newline}{newline}You can see your food reserve on the info bar. Hover over it to see how much food your party consumes each day. Since your party needs food, go to marketplace now to purchase some.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.BuyingFoodStep2** — Food items are also trade goods. You can find trade goods easily with the "Miscellaneous" filter.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.BuyingFoodStep3** — Grain is usually the cheapest food you can buy.{newline}{newline}Other types of food may grant various bonuses when consumed.{newline}{newline}Buy some food now.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ChoosingPerkUpgradesStep1** — Choosing Perk Upgrades

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ChoosingPerkUpgradesStep2** — Choosing Perk Upgrades

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ChoosingPerkUpgradesStep3** — Choosing Perk Upgrades

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ChoosingPerkUpgradesStep1** — When your skill points reach a required threshold, one or more perks will become available.{newline}{newline}This will be notified by a small indicator over the character screen button.{newline}{newline}Click on the character button to view available perk choices.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ChoosingPerkUpgradesStep1_controller** — When your skill points reach a required threshold, one or more perks will become available.{newline}{newline}This will be notified by a small indicator over the character screen button.{newline}{newline}Press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the character button to view available perk choices.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ChoosingPerkUpgradesStep2** — You can choose an available perk by clicking on its button.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ChoosingPerkUpgradesStep2_controller** — You can choose an available perk by pressing {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on its button.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ChoosingPerkUpgradesStep3** — Perks usually become available in pairs.{newline}{newline}Each one grants different bonuses so choose wisely.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ChoosingSkillFocusStep1** — Choosing Skill Focus

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ChoosingSkillFocusStep2** — Choosing Skill Focus

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ChoosingSkillFocusStep1** — You gain a level every time your total skill points total reaches a target value. Leveling up grants focus points to spend.{newline}{newline}If you have free focus points you will see it by a small indicator over the character screen button. Click on the button to review different skills and choose one to increase focus.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ChoosingSkillFocusStep1_controller** — You gain a level every time your total skill points total reaches a target value. Leveling up grants focus points to spend.{newline}{newline}If you have free focus points you will see it by a small indicator over the character screen button. Press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the character button to review different skills and choose one to increase focus.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ChoosingSkillFocusStep2** — Focus points are used to increase the learning rate at any skill.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.GettingCompanionsStep1** — Getting Companions

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.GettingCompanionsStep2** — Getting Companions

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.GettingCompanionsStep3** — Getting Companions

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GettingCompanionsStep1** — In towns, you can find talented individuals that can aid you.{newline}{newline}These potential companions can be found hanging out in taverns.{newline}{newline}Go to tavern district now to find a potential companion.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GettingCompanionsStep2** — You can see portraits of Important NPCs on the top bar.{newline}{newline}Click on the portrait and choose visit from the menu.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GettingCompanionsStep2_controller** — You can see portraits of Important NPCs on the top bar.{newline}{newline}Press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on their portrait and choose talk from the menu.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GettingCompanionsStep3** — Click on the "Visit" button to start conversation.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.GettingCompanionsStep3_controller** — Press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the "Visit" button to start conversation.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.RansomingPrisonersStep1** — Ransoming Prisoners

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.RansomingPrisonersStep2** — Ransoming Prisoners

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.RansomingPrisonersStep1** — You can ransom your prisoners off to the ransom broker.{newline}{newline}You can find him in the tavern area.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.RansomingPrisonersStep2** — You can sell off all prisoners at once.{newline}{newline}Or you can engage with the ransom broker to pick them individually.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EquipmentSets** — Equipment Sets

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EquipmentSets** — Every character in Calradia has three equipment sets for different purposes: Civilian, battle, and stealth. You can switch between their sets using the buttons over the character's model. Note that some equipment may be unusable in certain equipment sets, due to their intended environment.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.PartySpeed** — Overburdened

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.PartySpeed** — Notice your party speed has dropped because you are carrying too much.{newline}You should reduce the amount of weight you carry to speed up.{newline}You can also increase your party's carrying capacity by recruiting more troops or buying horses and camels.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ArmyCohesionStep1** — Army Cohesion

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ArmyCohesionStep2** — Army Cohesion

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ArmyCohesionStep1** — Notice how your army cohesion has dropped to a low point, and it is more likely that your army will disperse.{newline}You can click on the army management button to boost your cohesion.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ArmyCohesionStep1_controller** — Notice how your army cohesion has dropped to a low point, and it is more likely that your army will disperse.{newline}You can press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the army management button to boost your cohesion.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ArmyCohesionStep2** — You can click on "+" button to add 10 cohesion. Be aware that boosting it costs some influence.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ArmyCohesionStep2_controller** — You can press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the "+" button to add 10 cohesion. Be aware that boosting it costs some influence.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.CreateArmyStep1** — Creating Army

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.CreateArmyStep2** — Creating Army

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.CreateArmyStep3** — Creating Army

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.CreateArmyStep1** — You can call other lords to your banner. Click on the highlighted army icon on the lower right to do so.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.CreateArmyStep1_controller** — You can call other lords to your banner. Press {CONSOLE_ACTION_KEY} while the cursor is on the highlighted army icon on the lower right to do so.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.CreateArmyStep2** — You can create an army by adding members from the list on the left. To finalize your choices, press "Done".

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.CreateArmyStep3** — Gathering of your army may take some time.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.RaidVillageStep1** — Raiding Village

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.RaidVillageStep1** — Raiding villages will weaken the economy of the owner's faction by disrupting the flow of supplies between the village and its bound settlement. Also, the raiding party will get some resources from raiding.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.BombardmentStep1** — Sieges

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.BombardmentStep1** — Sieges are an integral part of warfare in Calradia, as they are the main way to conquer towns and castles.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.OrderOfBattleTutorialStep1** — Order of Battle

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.OrderOfBattleTutorialStep2** — Order of Battle

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.OrderOfBattleTutorialStep3** — Order of Battle

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderOfBattleTutorialStep1** — If you have at least 20 troops you'll have the option to draw up a strategy before every battle. You can assign heroes to be captains of formations, distribute your troops between formations and give preferences to which kinds of troops should be included in which formation, as well as some other options.{newline}{newline}Try assigning yourself as the captain of one of the formations by dragging your portrait at the center top to one of the formations' captain slots.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderOfBattleTutorialStep2** — You can create new formations to divide your troops into smaller groups to have finer control. You can also determine what percentage of the selected troop type should start the battle in these formations by manipulating the sliders inside the formation cards.{newline}{newline}Try creating a new formation by selecting its type and adjust a formation's troop weight.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.OrderOfBattleTutorialStep3** — If you're not the encounter leader, the Order of Battle screen will open in a limited state. This means that lords senior to you will choose their formations first. You then assign yourself to a formation, and you will control that single formation.{newline}{newline}Try assigning yourself to an available formation.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.CraftingStep1Tutorial** — Smithy

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.CraftingStep1Tutorial** — This screen allows you to craft different weapons for yourself or to fulfill orders for local non-player characters. To do this, you must use raw or refined resources that you can either purchase or manufacture by smelting weapons you carry.{newline}{newline}You can change the type of weapon that you are crafting through the highlighted button.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.CraftingOrdersTutorial** — Crafting orders

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.CraftingOrdersTutorial** — Notables in towns will post orders for new weapons. They'll have requirements for you to complete and they'll pay you for the ordered weapon.{newline}{newline}You can view these orders by clicking on the highlighted button, at the top right.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.InventoryBannerItemTutorial** — Banners

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.InventoryBannerItemTutorial** — You've found a banner! Banners are items that can be equipped by heroes and they give significant bonuses to the formations those heroes lead. You can inspect and see the effect of the banner by hovering over the banner item.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.CrimeTutorial** — Crime

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.CrimeTutorial** — This is your crime rating with the faction that owns the settlement. You gain a rating by robbing or attacking a kingdom's subjects. Players with a rating of 30 or higher in a neutral kingdom will be barred from its settlements, while an independent player with a crime rating of 60 or higher will be attacked on sight. Crime rating will decay over time.{newline}{newline}You can get more details on crime rating from the encyclopedia.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.AssignRolesTutorial** — Assign Roles

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.AssignRolesTutorial** — You can assign roles to your clan members in your party. They'll give bonuses according to their skills and perks.{newline}{newline}You can start the assignment process through the higlighted area.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.KingdomDecisionVotingTutorial** — Kingdom Decision

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.KingdomDecisionVotingTutorial** — You can participate in your faction's decision-making process through this panel. You can spend influence to sway opinions but the ruler will always have the last word.{newline}{newline}Select one of the available decision options to continue.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaHomeTutorial** — Encyclopedia

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaHomeTutorial** — Encyclopedia offers up-to-date information about settlements, heroes, clans, and factions. Select a category to see contents listed under the said category.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaSettlementsTutorial** — Encyclopedia Settlements

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaSettlementsTutorial** — The Encyclopedia has information on all the towns, castles, and villages of Calradia. Once visited or revealed, you can track up-to-date information from the encyclopedia.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaTroopsTutorial** — Encyclopedia Units

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaTroopsTutorial** — Troop pages allow you to see the skills and equipment sets of the selected troop. Try investigating upgrade trees to plan your army composition ahead of time.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaKingdomsTutorial** — Encyclopedia Kingdoms

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaKingdomsTutorial** — Investigate kingdoms to keep up with the fiefs, clans, and wars of the kingdoms of the Calradia.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaClansTutorial** — Encyclopedia Clans

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaClansTutorial** — Keeping up with Clans of Caldraia allows you to follow up on allies and foes alike. You can check their members, fiefs, and power levels upon reveal.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaConceptsTutorial** — Encyclopedia Concepts

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaConceptsTutorial** — Bannerlord has many different elements that affect the world of Calradia. You can always use filters to learn more about the game concepts.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaTrackTutorial** — Track

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaTrackTutorial** — Tracking allows you to find the settlements on the world map. As long as the track button is active location selected settlements will be highlighted. You can click the point near the settlement text to disable tracking.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaSearchTutorial** — Search

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaSearchTutorial** — If you know what or who you are looking for you can use the search bar and type in. The search bar lists all the persons, settlements, and troops of the Calradia.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaFiltersTutorial** — Filters

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaFiltersTutorial** — Trying to find something specific? Use filters on the left bar to narrow out the results.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaSortTutorial** — Sort

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaSortTutorial** — The sorting menu lets you sort your results based on different variables.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.EncyclopediaFogOfWarTutorial** — Fog of War

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.EncyclopediaFogOfWarTutorial** — You have opened a page where your character has very little information. Arriving at settlements and meeting people of interest related to this page will reveal more and up to date information.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_istiana** — Yes... Do I know you?

**str_comment_quest_taken.storymode_mentor** — Have you decided what to do?

**main_storyline_skip_tutorial_notification_text** — A few hours after you leave the training ground, you come across a wounded man lying under a tree. You share your water with him and try to dress his wounds as best as you can. He tells you he is a traveling doctor. To thank you for your help, he hands you a small bronze artifact which he says was once given to him in payment by a warrior who said only that it was related to 'Neretzes' Folly.' He suspects it might be of great value. You resolve to find out more.

**rescue_family_quest_let_go_radagos_quest_log** — You saved your brothers and sister, and you decided to let {RADAGOS.LINK} go...

**rescue_family_quest_execute_radagos_quest_log** — You saved your brothers and sister, and you decided to execute {RADAGOS.LINK} because he caused the death of your parents.

**rescue_family_quest_radagos_conversation_line_1** — We found your little brother and sister. But my former partner {HIDEOUT_BOSS.LINK} betrayed me. We came into his camp to negotiate the kids' release, and he seized us right then and there.[if:convo_angry_voice]

**rescue_family_quest_brother_conversation_line_1** — Yes, we are all fine. The little ones are scared but fine... We need to be quick and get the hell out of this place.[if:convo_calm_friendly][ib:confident]

**rescue_family_quest_brother_conversation_line_2** — I'll take them to the nearest fortress immediately. They will be safe there.

**rescue_family_quest_galter_conversation_player_line_1** — He led us here. Where are my brothers and my sister?

**rescue_family_quest_radagos_goodbye_conversation_line_1** — Well... Looks like we've gotten your kin back to you, so my end of our deal is complete. I'll be making myself scarce now.[ib:hip][if:convo_uncomfortable_voice]

**rescue_family_quest_radagos_goodbye_conversation_player_line_1** — Perhaps by saving my brother and sister you earned your life back. Very well, go now.

**find_hideout_quest_radagos_conversation_line_1** — Good Heaven, I'll need a better description than that. My men have harvested dozens of little brats in this region. Quite good hunting grounds! Already sent most of them south to a slave market I know, though.[ib:hip][if:convo_snide_voice]

**find_hideout_quest_radagos_conversation_line_2** — Oh, you'll need my help all right, if you want to get them back - alive, that is.

**find_hideout_quest_radagos_conversation_line_3** — See, my boys have some pretty specific instructions about what to do if there's a rescue attempt...

**find_hideout_quest_brother_conversation_line_1** — I have a better idea. We would have a better chance if we split up now. I'll take {RADAGOS.NAME} and go find the slaver market and look for a way to free the children.[if:convo_normal]

**find_hideout_quest_brother_conversation_line_2** — However we must be careful not to endanger their lives and it could be better to just buy them. We need to have our purses full for that though.

**find_hideout_quest_brother_conversation_line_3** — Get on the road now. Once I locate the little ones, I'll come find you.[ib:normal][if:convo_calm_friendly]

**little_sister_encyclopedia_text** — {PLAYER_LITTLE_SISTER.NAME} is the little sister of {PLAYER.LINK}. She has been abducted by bandits, who intend to sell her into slavery.

## NavalDLC / War Sails Dialogue Strings
*Source: `NavalDLC/ModuleData/naval_dialog_strings.xml` — 194 entries*

**str_comment_endplayerbattle_you_defeated_our_enemy_at_sea.default** — I heard you fought ship to ship with {DEFEATED_PARTY_LEADER}, and won.

**str_comment_endplayerbattle_we_defeated_enemy_at_sea.default** — I will not forget how our ships met those of {DEFEATED_PARTY_LEADER}, and bested them.

**str_comment_endplayerbattle_we_defeated_pirates.default** — We did well to defeat those pirates back there. The common enemy of mankind, so they say.

**str_comment_endplayerbattle_we_defeated_pirates.default_2** — We did well to defeat those pirates back there. The common enemy of mankind, so they say.

**str_comment_endplayerbattle_you_accosted_my_trading_ship.default** — I hear you seized one of my trading vessels. I am not pleased.

**str_comment_endplayerbattle_we_defeated_you_at_sea.default** — I remember when we last met and battled, ship to ship.

**str_comment_endplayerbattle_we_were_defeated_at_sea.default** — I remember when you and I last fought together. We had good ships and valiant crews. It's a pity we did not prevail.

**str_comment_intro.common_cautious_at_sea** — I shall mark down your name. Now, do not take it amiss if I do not invite you to dine on board, for the world is a treacherous place, and I have learned to be wary.

**str_surrender_demand_hero.curt_at_sea** — You can't outrun us. Yield or die.[ib:warrior][if:convo_aggressive]

**str_surrender_demand_hero.earnest_at_sea** — Strike your sails and ship your oars, or we shall attack.[ib:warrior][if:convo_angry]

**str_surrender_demand_hero.softspoken_at_sea** — Heave to and prepare to be boarded, or fight.[ib:warrior][if:convo_angry]

**str_surrender_demand_hero.ironic_at_sea** — Right. So unless you ship your oars now and let us board you, you're going down.[ib:warrior][if:convo_angry]

**str_piracy_threat.1** — Ahoy there! There's a tax on ships in these waters, sailor, paid either in coin or in blood.[if:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_piracy_threat.2** — You! Heave to, you bastards, or we'll cut every last one of your throats.[if:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_piracy_threat.3** — Ahoy there. Furl your sails and ship your oars.[if:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_piracy_pay_agreement.1** — Oh aye, you can buy your lives. I wouldn't push too hard on the price if I were you, though, as you might say it's a bit of a seller's market.[ib:hip][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_piracy_pay_agreement.2** — Name the sum, and be quick about it, or we'll just feed you to the sharks.[ib:hip][rf:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_piracy_pay_agreement.3** — Good, good. I much prefer a straight-up deal to rummaging through your gut afterward to see what you might have hid there.[ib:hip][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_piracy_conclusion.1** — Very well. Sail safely, and don't forget to put aside some silver for your return trip.[ib:closed][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_piracy_conclusion.2** — We'll take it. Now best get your sails over the horizon before we change your minds.[ib:closed][rf:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_piracy_conclusion.3** — Good. Now be careful out there. World's full of thieves, not all of them as kind as we are.[ib:closed][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_piracy_start_fight.1** — Well, let no one say we didn't give you a chance.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_annoyed]

**str_piracy_start_fight.2** — Expect no mercy.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_very_stern]

**str_piracy_start_fight.3** — Really? I suppose I'll be getting my hands dirty today, then.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_culture_rich_name.nord** — Nords

**str_culture_description.nord** — The Nords are a people made by the sea. The very name of their home, the Nordvyg, refers to the icy stretch of glacier-cut coastline that links their scattered settlements. Until recently, their towns were little more than a shrine or market beside a fjord or estuary, surrounded by a palisade. Some make a modest living by farming barley and raising sheep, but those with ambition must venture forth in their longships to trade, plunder or fight for hire.

**str_comment_noble_introduces_self.nord** — I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK} of the {CLAN_NAME}.

**str_liege_title.nord** — king of the Nordvyg

**str_liege_title_female.nord** — queen of the Nordvyg

**str_comment_noble_introduces_self_and_clan.nord** — I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}, one of the ancient lineages of the Nords.

**str_comment_noble_introduces_self_and_clan.nord_boasting** — I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}. One table in the High Hall is reserved for our fallen, and two more for those we have slain.

**str_comment_noble_introduces_self_and_clan.nord_individualist_female** — I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}. I will not boast to you of my lineage. In the north, we aim to surpass the fame of our forefathers, not live off of their reputation.

**str_comment_noble_introduces_self_and_clan.nord_individualist** — I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}. I will not boast to you of my lineage. A true son of the North aims to surpass his fathers, not live off of their reputation.

**str_comment_noble_introduces_self_and_clan.nord_boasting_curt** — I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}. We are wound-smiths and wave-riders, raven-feeders and ring-breakers.

**str_comment_noble_introduces_self_and_clan.nord_boasting_ironic** — I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}. It is unseemly to boast, so I will leave it to others to tell you of our deeds. It is a conversation best had on a long winter's night, for it may take some considerable time.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_nord_0n** — Some day I hope to tell my story to a dozen of my sons, as we feast for the solstice in my hall, so that they shall follow my example and sail out into the world to make their fortunes. Until then, I will settle for telling it to strangers in taverns like yourself.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_nord_0n** — I was the youngest in my family. My mother always told me that some day I would own the finest galley in the northlands. My oldest brother heard this, and would mock me incessantly. When I would set forth on my fine ship? Would my mother sail with me to fight my enemies? Perhaps he wished me to shame me into leaving, so I would give him no trouble about our inheritance.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_nord_0n** — One day, soon after I came of age, I took a hundred sheep from our flocks, sold them, and bought a small snekya. I hired some men too, and set off to raid the coast of Sturgia. But of course I was a poor judge of warriors, and when the boyar's druzhina set upon us they scattered, and burned my ship.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_nord_0n** — I have sworn that I shall not return home, unless I am indeed standing at the helm of a fine ship that my brother could envy. I have fought for Vlandian barons, imperial archons, even once an noyan of the east. I have fought in many battles, some on land and some at sea. But lords are stingy, and I think none has rewarded me according to my due.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_nord_0n** — Nothing makes a finer warrior than a hunger to prove yourself that can never be satisfied.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_nord_0n** — I wonder how many men you have slain to forget a child's taunt.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_nord_0n** — So... Perhaps you have a need of warriors, or captains for your ships. If you are a generous lord, then I can be a worthy follower.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_nord_0n** — I was the youngest son in my family. Well, in our lands, sons - especially the youngest - are expected to make their own name. I can fight by land or by sea, and I am ready to serve whoever rewards me well.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_nord_1n** — I seek work. I will tell you my story, so that you are in no doubt of my skills.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_nord_1n** — I come from Svalfjord. Farther north than that, people cannot live. There is ice in our bay for six months of the year. In the summer we hunt whales, black whales, which are smaller than most but are cunning and can still sink you if you're not careful. Each summer we gather in our boats and drive the whales into the fjord. Since I was a girl I would go with my father and uncle and several others from the village.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_nord_1n** — There was a dispute over a whale carcass. I do not remember what caused it, exactly, but my father felt he had sole claim to it. He cursed the others and said words that could not be unsaid. He would not apologize, and had to leave the village. So it was just me, him and my uncle, living alone on the coast, in a shelter dug into the turf with a hole in the roof to let out smoke.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_nord_1n** — My father insisted that we would still hunt. It was madness, just three people in a boat, but what else could we do? One day a whale that he harpooned dragged us far out to sea. When we were struggling to row back, a storm blew up, and sank the boat. My father and I swam ashore but my uncle drowned. I'd had enough. I left the next day.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_nord_1n** — Some men persist in folly unto death, and there is nothing you can do.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_nord_1n** — Where I come from, parents are to be honored and obeyed.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_nord_1n** — So... I can cast a harpoon, and handle a boat that is being dragged by a whale in its death throes. I think I would be of use in any ship's crew, if the pay is right.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_nord_1n** — I am from the Svalfjord, the further reaches of the Nordlands. We hunt whales in small boats. We trust our lives to each other's skill. If you have a ship to crew, you will find no one better.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_nord_2n** — I was born in a farm near Throndelag, but my family moved to the new lands near the Jumne river. If I see neither place again as long as I live, I will have no regret.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_nord_2n** — We moved to the Jumne because we heard there was farmland for the taking. When we arrived, we found there were Vanni already there, but at first they did not mind our presence. They lived in the woods and left us the open meadows by the river. I was given in marriage to the Vanni chieftain's son to seal the arrangement, along with some cloth and axe-heads.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_nord_2n** — More Nords followed, however. I was living in my husband's village, and the Vanni complained that the coming and going ruined the hunting. They thought this voided the deal. There were talks, but they went nowhere. So the Vanni killed some Nords in the fields - though not my brothers, as a consideration to me.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_nord_2n** — The Vanni hoped the other Nords would flee. But they did not know them. One of my brothers came to me in secret. He told me to poison my Vanni husband's family, like I was that old queen of Sturgland. Hah! One day my family demands that I wed this man and have his children, the next they say to kill him? I wasn't having it. I slipped off that night, and wish to see neither brothers nor husband again.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_nord_2n** — Yes, certainly family can be demanding...

**response_2.spc_wanderer_nord_2n** — Hmf. Without kin, we are as beasts.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_nord_2n** — At any rate, a year with the Vanni has taught me much about the woods, about herbs, the treatment of wounds and fevers. I reckon I could be of good use to a company of warriors.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_nord_2n** — I am from the Jumne. Although I am Nord by birth, I have lived among the Vanni. I know much about herbs, and the art of healing.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_nord_3n** — You want to hear a story, eh? I'll tell you the short version. The long, well, that could keep a longhouse entertained for a half-dozen midwinter nights. Beinlandings... In matters of the law, they don't like to make things simple. Or cheap.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_nord_3n** — See, I came to Beinland some years ago, like many from the Nordvyg. Land for the taking, they said, and all men stand equal before the law. I found one unsettled valley with a stream and lush grass, and built my home there. I should have asked why no one done so before.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_nord_3n** — Turns out my neighbor, Odig, was a difficult one. People say he had troll-blood. One day he shows up with his retainers and tells me my sheep had broken into his fields, when they hadn't, and demanded compensation. I told him to go away. Then I started to find my sheep dead in their pastures, and then one of my herdsman. I decided to take my case before the Thing.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_nord_3n** — The Thinglaw, though... To gain a hearing I needed a chieftain to back my case. I found one, but he brought a great retinue along with him, which I had to feast. The Thing ruled in my favor and outlawed Odig - everyone hated him - but to enforce the judgment , to take his head and his property, well, I was on my own there. My chief offered to provide armed men, but not for free.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_nord_3n** — Sounds like a fine source of income for the old clans of Beinland.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_nord_3n** — Just get yourself a lord and master. Much simpler than setting your own course though this world.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_nord_3n** — By then I had quite a few debts. Well, I sold my herd and my farmhouse to pay my creditors, and here I am, looking for a new source of income. I'll miss Beinland though. Herding in the lonely moors, hunting in the quiet woods. I like to roam the land, and if you're looking for a man to scout ahead, well, I may be him.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_nord_3n** — I'm from the Nordvyg, but moved to Beinland. I bought a herd of sheep there, which I hoped would make my fortune, but between several bad winters and some disputes with my neighbors, well, that all came to naught. I'm much poorer than I was before, but at least I'm a bit wiser for having studied at the foot of such a harsh teacher as that island. If you're looking for someone to lead your company through the wilds, well, I may be him.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_nord_4n** — So... What am I doing in this dingy tavern, far from my homeland? Well, I suppose it's because I was taught that it's a fine thing to be ambitious, to seize what chances fate gives you...

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_nord_4n** — I was sent by my village as a fyrdman to our jarl, Grykka Half-an-Ear. I was eager to fight and win wealth and glory, but I knew a bit about metalwork and he needed a smith, so instead of joining his warriors they put me in a sooty alcove at the base of the wall and told to pump the bellows and hammer nails and horseshoes.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_nord_4n** — But a smith's life has its advantages. The ladies of the castle, you see, sometimes needed their jewelry repaired. I was down there hammering away in the sweat and the smoke, and I suppose I was one of the few interesting things to see in that freezing fortress if you're a jarl's daughter with a great deal of time on her hands.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_nord_4n** — But you know what complications can come of love. The daughter was late in her time, and soon people would be asking questions. I helped myself to a blade and a horse in place of my long-unpaid wages and rode away as fast as I could. Maybe I'll go back 20 years from now and greet the new jarl with a cheerful, 'Hello, son!'

**response_1.spc_wanderer_nord_4n** — I suppose you owed nothing to a master who took you for granted.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_nord_4n** — Only a scoundrel would boast of such base behavior.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_nord_4n** — So, I don't mind sharpening blades and fixing armor, but the one thing I ask is the chance to better myself. Now that I've laid that out straight, what do you say? Do you have work for a man like me?

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_nord_4n** — My father was a smith, and I learned his trade. I know such skills are in high demand. I will gladly sharpen blades and repair armor for my pay, but the one thing I ask from any master is the chance to rise in the world.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_nord_5n** — Very well, then. I was a shipmaster. I'm Nord by birth but I've sailed mostly with the Khuzaits.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_nord_5n** — I grew up near Gauksdal, where my father was a ferry-man on the Jumne River. In those days the Khan was fighting the Sturgians on the great lakes. Not many of his followers had much experience with ships, and he was paying good wages, far more than our jarl would have. So, I went south..

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_nord_5n** — They put me as steersman on a qalguk. That was quite a jump, from a ferry-boat to the pride of the Khan's fleet, but I got the hang of it soon enough. Strange ship, the qalguk... Damned fast, but sluggish. I'd line it up for a run at our foes and we'd come down on them and shower them with arrows. Then we'd put about, make our way upwind, and do it again. We won a great battle in Laconis and captured two of their lodyas packed with loot.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_nord_5n** — Then the Khan settled things with the Sturgians and we went to war with the Empire. That didn't go as well. The dromons caught us one day on the Davana River, as we were sailing back from a raid. The tactics we used against the Sturgians... you can't do that in the confines of a river. Our ships got all jammed together and their ballistae set our sails on fire. I jumped and swam to shore but all my loot went down with the ship.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_nord_5n** — A commander must choose his battlefield carefully, on sea as much as on land.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_nord_5n** — Hah! This is what happens when horse-nomads mess about with boats.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_nord_5n** — So... I'm starting anew, with empty pockets. What do you say? Do you need a shipmaster? Perhaps I'll have better luck with you than I did on that qalguk.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_nord_5n** — I'm a steersman. I've served under several masters, and handled everything from small knarrs to big dromakions and qalguks in my time.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_nord_6n** — I served on the imperial navy for 10 years, on a dromon. If you're looking to hire someone, perhaps I can tell you about my experience.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_nord_6n** — Some years back, in the time of Neretzes, a group of us from Thronderlag crossed the Byalic to sign up with the Empire. I'll never forget my first sight of Diathma, those shining stone towers rising out of the lake. We docked next to a dromon, the Glory of the Senate. I looked up at the well-scrubbed decks, the polished oaken swan figurehead at the prow... It made our knarr look like a battered old toy. I signed on, then and there.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_nord_6n** — We had a good captain. He didn't care if you were Calradic or Nord, just that you put your back into your work. After three years they made me first mate. We sailed mostly in the Perassic, fighting the Aserai. Their ghurabs were almost as big as our dromons, with rams and ballistae. In that kind of fight every little advantage counts, so I made sure that every man knew his duty, our bowstrings were stored dry, and our stocks of bolts were full.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_nord_6n** — But then Neretzes died at Pendraic and the Empire ran out of money. Our pay was always late. Men got surly and shirked their duty. We got a new captain, too, who cursed us as blackguards and whipped us for little things. Each time we put into port a few jumped ship. We were too short-handed to caulk properly, and the Perassic shipworms rotted our timbers. It was only a matter of time before our timbers gave out in a storm, so I too left.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_nord_6n** — The imperial fleet in its prime must have been a sight to see. A sad fate.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_nord_6n** — So, when the Empire could no longer plunder at will, its splendor faded. Divine justice, I say.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_nord_6n** — So I'm done with the Empire... But I'm not done with the sea. If you've got a ship, and you're looking for a man who can keep it battle-ready, you might give me consideration..

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_nord_6n** — I was a boatswain in the imperial navy. If you need someone to keep a crew disciplined and a ship battle-ready, I'm your man.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_nord_7n** — Aye, I can do that. I was a pirate, a sea-raider, a plague on the oceans, the common enemy of all mankind, and a damned fine time I had.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_nord_7n** — I was one of a group of lads who used to spend time with our jarl's youngest son. We'd hunt together, drink together, raise hell together... Eventually though he spent his way through his inheritance, so he sailed off with one of his father's longships, bringing us along for the ride.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_nord_7n** — We cruised from Beinland down to the Biscan coast and back, looking sharp for merchantmen and gave warships a wide berth. Sometimes our prey had some fight in her, and I don't mind telling you that I had a real knack for keeping my footing on a tossing cog as we traded blows with the crew. But most of the time we'd just leap aboard, leering and swearing we'd drink from their skulls, and they paid us to be on our way.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_nord_7n** — 'A short life, but a merry one!' we'd say, and that's how it went. We'd put into a cove to celebrate the capture of a corbita. I'd had some poorly salted fish though, so while my friends were carousing I was curled up sick in a sea-cave. I staggered out at dawn to find a Vlandian baron and his knights had come upon my shipmates in the night, when they were in their cups, and left them all headless on the beach.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_nord_7n** — Well... It sounds like you've got luck, which is a good thing to have.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_nord_7n** — Thank the Heavens, which saved you from a life of villainy and gave you another chance.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_nord_7n** — I can't curse fate, we all knew how it would end, but it did leave me without a source of drinking money. So... I'm a good fighter at sea, and I know a thing or two about pirates and rogues, and how to handle them. You have any ships that need an extra hand?

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_nord_7n** — Aye, well, I used to be one of those who you might call Sea Raiders. Our ship was taken, though, and I was the sole survivor. I'm on the lookout for honest work, or work of another kind, if you know a captain who's hiring.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_aserai_0n** — I can only hope that Heaven has prepared a reward for all the sorrow and suffering that I am about to relate to you.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_aserai_0n** — I am a skilled mariner. I am from Quyaz. The blood of the Kannic people runs in my veins, and Kannic blood is half saltwater, so they say. I took to the sea at an early age as a navigator's apprentice, and by 20 I had accumulated enough to buy a share in a ship sailing the Jade Sea.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_aserai_0n** — Alas, our captain was a braggart. We were headed to Revyl with a cargo of dates and dyes. He wished to show his knowledge of the Bay of Ortygia, and took a quick route between the islands. Of course he was dashed on the rocks. I seized a timber, and was washed shore with a dozen other half-drowned survivors who had what I guess you could call luck.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_aserai_0n** — My next voyage was on a felucca out of Zeonica heading eastward to Danustica. Pirates took us, and burnt it to the waterline. Then I took service on a dromon, fitted as a privateer, but we were caught by an unseasonal dust-storm that rolled off the Jabal Tamar and smashed us into a rock in the Gulf of Charas. Each time, destiny saw fit to spare me after first having paupered me.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_aserai_0n** — Great are your sorrows, but greater still your perseverance! Surely it shall be rewarded with riches.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_aserai_0n** — Yeah, okay, maybe also consider that your destiny wants you to remain on dry land.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_aserai_0n** — Despite my sufferings I still yearn for travel and traffic. And none of these wrecks was any fault of my own. Misfortune is a good teacher, they say, and I think my knowledge is second to none in terms of what not to do when in command of a ship.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_aserai_0n** — I'm a sailor out of Quyaz. We venture further from our homes than anyone else on the coast, and I believe that my knowledge of winds, currents and stars is the equal of any of my peers.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_empire_0n** — Let me think how I want to put this...

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_empire_0n** — I'm from Zeonica. In my youth, the archon was one Sulvanis, father of the current Garios. Now, let us say your empire is at peace with the Aserai and Vlandians, but their merchants are cutting into your pockets and you expect to be at war in the future. If one of your mariners sailed out of harbor with one ship and came back with two, would you question them too carefully?

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_empire_0n** — So here's where I come in... Let's say you have acquired a cheap Aserai shabak, by one means or the other. It was intended as a ship that could move goods from one place to another as cheaply as possible. But you want it refitted to be faster, with a lead-sheeted belly and some towers for archers, never mind why. My family and I specialized in adding them.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_empire_0n** — But suppose again that you are the archon Garios, scheming to become emperor. You need a treaty with the sultan, sooner not later. And the sultan has his court full of aggrieved merchants. So you announce a list of men to be exiled, names that are known throughout the Perassic Sea as men of ingenuity and daring.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_empire_0n** — No nation ever prospered on the seas without a bit of corsairing.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_empire_0n** — Pirates, and those that help them, are the common enemy of mankind.

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_empire_0n** — I will say this. Many lords condemn us, but relatively few are willing to pass up the opportunity to employ us, at least not when they have ships to maintain.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_empire_0n** — I grew up in Zeonica. Corsairing is an honorable profession there. It hones the skills of the empire's sailors, between wars. I specialize in the construction and modification of corsair vessels, and may even have sailed on one from time to time.

**prebackstory.spc_wanderer_vlandia_0n** — I am from Charas. I don't know how much you know of its recent past.

**backstory_a.spc_wanderer_vlandia_0n** — My father was one of the Sea-Victuallers. Perhaps you have heard of them. When the guildmaster of Charas brought in the Brotherhood of the Woods and rebelled against the Vlandian king, the fishermen of the coast brought supplies to the besieged city. They did it for pay, mind, as starving cities will pay dearly for moldy bread and minnows, not because they believed a word of the Brotherhood's mad promises of a world without lords and ladies and taxes and tithes.

**backstory_b.spc_wanderer_vlandia_0n** — But the Baron dey Cortain, who led the siege, wasn't terribly interested in their reasons. He went up and down the coast, hanging anyone with a boat with five leagues of Charas who could not give a full account of himself. An informant put my father's name on the list, and so we like so many others fled to the islands of the gulf.

**backstory_c.spc_wanderer_vlandia_0n** — So that's where I grew up on, on a gull-splattered bit of rock, living on fish and seaweed and rainwater, because of course the baron's informant had taken my family's land in his absence. But I can safely say that no one knows the sea like I do, as the wind can come at you hard from any direction at any time of day, and a fisherman who can't slip between two rocks a stone's throw apart with a breeze hard on his beam is food for the sharks.

**response_1.spc_wanderer_vlandia_0n** — A cruel fate to suffer, just for bring food to your fellow-men.

**response_2.spc_wanderer_vlandia_0n** — What is it with the fishermen of Charas? Are there no fish left to catch, that they must profit from smuggling and rebellion?

**backstory_d.spc_wanderer_vlandia_0n** — At any rate, if you are looking for a helmsman, I doubt you will find a better one.

**generic_backstory.spc_wanderer_vlandia_0n** — I am from Charas. The islands of the coast are rich in mackeral and tuna but treacherous, with many small currents and unpredictable winds. We reckon ourselves the finest sailors in Calradia, if you don't mind my saying.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_cu_at_sea** — Ahoy! I want to speak to your captain.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_rude_cu_at_sea** — Ahoy! Damn your eyes and stay out of our way, you clumsy lubbers. Who captains you?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_under_command_cu_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... Our ship is at your command.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_attacking_cu_at_sea** — Who are you? Strike your sails and ship your oars, or prepare to fight.

**str_context_line.impolite_cu** — {STR_SALUTATION}... Is that you? Please be brief. The winds are with us and I have no time to waste.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_iu_default_at_sea** — Ahoy, there! May I have the pleasure of knowing who captains this vessel?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_iu_rude_at_sea** — Ahoy, there! If you could be so kind, could you try to steer your lump of flotsam out of our way?

**str_context_line.attacking_unmet_iu_at_sea** — Ahoy! As it appears your poor floundering tub can't outrun us, we might as well have a little chat. Perhaps you'd like to introduce yourself?

**str_context_line.friendly_iu_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... Ahoy! So somehow you've managed to keep yourself afloat since we last met. It's good to see you, you worthless lubber!

**str_context_line.first_meeting_v1_weary_iu_at_sea** — Ahoy! What's your name? Forgive me if we have spoken before and I do not recall, for I have met many promising captains only to hear later they were swallowed by the deep.

**str_context_line.enemy_but_not_attacking_iu_at_sea** — Ahoy, there! I know you. Be careful, now, as you might find that you've caught a bigger fish than you first reckoned.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_earnest_eu_at_sea** — Ahoy! Greetings to you! May I ask who captains this vessel?

**str_context_line.attacking_unmet_eu_at_sea** — Ahoy! Do you care to tell me your name, before I give the order to engage your ship?

**str_context_line.attacking_unmet_v2_honorable_eu_at_sea** — Ahoy! Respect the custom of the sea and the terms of parley, and I shall do likewise. Now, who are you?

**str_context_line.dislike_eu_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... Pirates like you may put on airs, but they all end up the same way, dangling from the yardarm of their betters.

**str_context_line.friendly_eu_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... Ahoy! I hope you have been enjoying fair weather and good seas.

**str_context_line.attacking_gloat_eu_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... Is that you? It doesn't look like you can escape your fate, does it? Let's see if the sea accepts your vile corpse, or if it just vomits it back up.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_wary_su_at_sea** — Ahoy! If you can hear me at that distance, come no further. Whose ship is this?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_wary_v1_su_at_sea** — Ahoy! We know you're an enemy, so do not think to take us unawares.

**str_context_line.attacking_unmet_su_at_sea** — Ahoy! You appear be a foe, and in a minute I will order my ship to close with you and take you. But first, I would know your name.

**str_context_line.under_command_su** — {STR_SALUTATION}... My ship and crew are yours to command.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_default_cl_at_sea** — Ahoy! Whose ship is this?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_wary_cl_at_sea** — Ahoy! Keep a bowshot's length away, or more, until I know if you're friend or foe.

**str_context_line.attacking_unmet_cl_at_sea** — Ahoy! Who are you? Speak, before I send you to the bottom.

**str_context_line.enemy_met_cl_at_sea** — Ahoy! You want something with us? You might find you've caught more than you bargained for.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_il_at_sea** — Ahoy! So, who captains this here wallowing sow of a vessel?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_attacking_il_at_sea** — Ahoy! If have anything to say, then say it. But try anything tricky and we'll send you right to the bottom.

**str_context_line.attacking_v2_cruel_il_at_sea** — Well, I'll not deny it. It'll be a real pleasure to feed you to the sharks.

**str_context_line.friendly_met_il_at_sea** — Ahoy! {STR_SALUTATION}... I'd know your vessel anywhere! Look at the state of that ship. I'm surprised it doesn't just sink into the sea out of shame.

**str_context_line.unmet_el_at_sea** — Ahoy! ... What ship is this, and who's the captain?

**str_context_line.attacking_unmet_el_at_sea** — Ahoy there, now! Before we fight, if you will, tell me who captains your ship!

**str_context_line.metbefore_el_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... Is that you on that ship? It's been a while.

**str_context_line.dislike_el_at_sea** — Ahoy! I know you, don't I? {STR_SALUTATION}... Do you and I have anything to talk about?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_sl_at_sea** — Ahoy! May I speak to your captain?

**str_context_line.metbefore_friendly_sl_at_sea** — Ahoy! Is that you, {STR_SALUTATION}? It's good to see you.

**str_context_line.attacking_sl_at_sea** — Ahoy! Do you wish to speak, before we attack?

**str_context_line.dislike_sl_at_sea** — Ahoy! I know your ship. {STR_SALUTATION}, isn't it? Do you and I have anything to talk about?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_ct_at_sea** — I do not know your ship. Who commands you?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_wary_cu_at_sea** — Ahoy! Keep your distance, lest you foul our sails. Who is in command over there?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_attracted_male_ct_at_sea** — Greetings! Do I speak to the captain of this ship, my lady?

**str_context_line.attacking_cruel_ct_at_sea** — Who captains this ship? I would know whom I slay.

**str_context_line.attacking_met_cruel_ct_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... I shall stain the seas with your blood.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_it_at_sea_exaggerated** — You, over there! With which bold seafarer do I have the pleasure of speaking?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_it_at_sea_sarcastic** — You, over there! Tell me the name of the captain brave enough to put to sea in such a leaky jumble of planks as your ship.

**str_context_line.friendly_it_at_sea** — I trust you have been keeping well, enjoying the salt air and sending the miscreants of the sea to their watery graves.

**str_context_line.attacking_1_it_at_sea** — Well... Unless I reckon the odds falsely, I'd say you have a good chance of getting wet shortly. I hope you can swim.

**str_context_line.friendly_il_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}! When I saw that hull all covered with barnacles, those tangled ropes, that cluttered deck, I knew it must be you!

**str_context_line.first_meeting_et_at_sea** — Peace to you, stranger, and fair seas. I do not know your ship. To whom do I speak?

**str_context_line.first_meeting_enemy_et_at_sea** — I do not know your ship. Who are you? What do you want with us?

**str_context_line.attacking_unmet_et_at_sea** — You, over there! Who commands you? Know that we mean to take you or to sink you.

**str_context_line.friendly_et_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... Peace to you... I hope the sea air is doing you good.

**str_context_line.attacking_met_hostile_et_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... The seas have delivered you into our hands.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_st_at_sea** — You, over there! Peace to you! Who captains your ship?

**str_context_line.friendly_st_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... I hope the seas have been treating you well.

**str_context_line.firstmeeting_attacking_cruel_st_at_sea** — I don't know you... If you have anything to say, say it quickly. The sharks are hungry and I would not keep them waiting.

**str_context_line.attacking_hate_st_at_sea** — I've waited a long time for this day. Have a good look around you, for soon your eyes will have little to see but the inside of a shark's belly.

**str_context_line.first_meeting_under_command_st_at_sea** — {STR_SALUTATION}... We sail at your command.

**main_storyline_skip_tutorial_notification_text** — A few hours after you leave the training ground, you come across a wounded man lying under a tree. He says he too was attacked by bandits. You share your water with him and try to dress his wounds as best as you can. He tells you he is a traveling doctor. To thank you for your help, he hands you a small bronze artifact which he says was once given to him in payment by a warrior who said only that it was related to 'Neretzes' Folly.' He suspects it might be of great value. You resolve to find out more. The doctor gives you one more bit of information. He overheard the bandits talking about captives they had seized on their raids. They planned to part ways, with one group taking their prisoners to the south, and the other planning to head northwest to sell them to pirates at the port of Ostican. You may be able to help your brother by searching there for your siblings.

**rescue_family_quest_let_go_radagos_quest_log** — You saved your brothers, and you decided to let {RADAGOS.LINK} go...

**rescue_family_quest_execute_radagos_quest_log** — You saved your brothers, and you decided to execute {RADAGOS.LINK} because he caused the death of your parents.

**rescue_family_quest_radagos_conversation_line_1** — We found your little brother. But my former partner {HIDEOUT_BOSS.LINK} betrayed me. We came into his camp to negotiate the boy’s release, and he seized us right then and there.[if:convo_angry_voice]

**rescue_family_quest_brother_conversation_line_1** — Yes, we are all fine. {LITTLE_BROTHER.NAME} is scared but fine... We need to be quick and get the hell out of this place.[if:convo_calm_friendly][ib:confident]

**rescue_family_quest_brother_conversation_line_2** — I'll take him to the nearest fortress immediately. He will be safe there.

**rescue_family_quest_galter_conversation_player_line_1** — He led us here. Where are my brothers?

**rescue_family_quest_radagos_goodbye_conversation_line_1** — Well... Looks like we've gotten your brother back to you, so my end of our deal is complete. I'll be making myself scarce now.[ib:hip][if:convo_uncomfortable_voice]

**rescue_family_quest_radagos_goodbye_conversation_player_line_1** — Perhaps by saving my brother you earned your life back. Very well, go now.

**find_hideout_quest_radagos_conversation_line_1** — Good Heaven, I’ll need a better description than that. My men have harvested dozens of little brats in this region. Quite good hunting grounds! Sold some of them to some pirates from Ostican, and sent the rest south to a slave market I know, though.[ib:hip][if:convo_snide_voice]

**find_hideout_quest_radagos_conversation_line_2** — Oh, you'll need my help all right, if you want to get them back - alive, that is. See, my boys have some pretty specific instructions about what to do if there's a rescue attempt...

**find_hideout_quest_radagos_conversation_line_3** — Also, I’ll be straight with you, seeing as you’ll find out soon enough anyway. If I recall right, we already sold off your sister to those pirates in Ostican. I remember faces well, you see, and one of them looked a bit like you. So… Here’s what I can do for you. With luck, I can help you get your brother back. Your sister – well, I know nothing of ships and the sea, so I couldn’t tell you where they might have taken her. I’m sorry, but I won’t promise you what I can’t deliver.

**find_hideout_quest_brother_conversation_line_1** — I have a better idea. We would have a better chance if we split up now. I’ll take {RADAGOS.NAME} and go find the slaver market. You might wish to make inquiries in Ostican. It’s a port town, so they might have sailed on from there.

**find_hideout_quest_brother_conversation_line_2** — In either case, we must be careful not to endanger their lives and it could be better to just buy them. We need to have our purses full for that though.

**find_hideout_quest_brother_conversation_line_3** — Get on the road now, and if you get a chance, start making inquiries at Ostican for {LITTLE_SISTER.NAME}. Once I locate {LITTLE_BROTHER.NAME}, I'll come find you.[ib:normal][if:convo_calm_friendly]

**little_sister_encyclopedia_text** — {PLAYER_LITTLE_SISTER.NAME} is the little sister of {PLAYER.NAME}. She was abducted by bandits and sold to a confederation of pirates and slave-traders known as the Sea Hounds.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipControlTutorial** — Ship Controls

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipControlTutorial** — To control a ship, you must go to its command point and interact with it by pressing {INTERACTION_KEY}.{newline}{newline}This will let you control the ship, by using {FORWARD_KEY}, {LEFT_KEY}, {BACKWARDS_KEY}, {RIGHT_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipControlTutorial_controller** — To control a ship, you must go to its command point and interact with it by pressing {INTERACTION_KEY}.{newline}{newline}This will let you control the ship, by using {CONSOLE_MOVEMENT_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipSailTutorial** — Ship Controls

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipSailTutorial** — To use the wind as efficiently as possible, check the ship widget in the lower right of your screen. The wind dial displays the direction of the wind - try to keep it within the green zones to generate the most forward force.{newline}{newline}Press {TOGGLE_SAIL_KEY} to unfurl the sail of your ship.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipOarsmanTutorial** — Ship Controls

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipOarsmanTutorial** — In order to change your active oarsman amount, press {TOGGLE_OARSMEN_KEY}.{newline}{newline}Now assign your entire crew to your oars. You can check your current oarsman status in the widget next to your health bar.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipCameraTutorial** — Ship Controls

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipCameraTutorial** — There are several different camera perspectives for your ship.{newline}{newline}Try switching between them by pressing {TOGGLE_CAMERA_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipCloseSailTutorial** — Ship Controls

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipCloseSailTutorial** — When you want to slow down, you can furl your sails by pressing {TOGGLE_SAIL_KEY} again.{newline}{newline}You can also use your oarsmen by pressing {BACKWARDS_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipCloseSailTutorial_controller** — When you want to slow down, you can furl your sails by pressing {TOGGLE_SAIL_KEY} again.{newline}{newline}You can also use your oarsmen via {CONSOLE_MOVEMENT_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipBoardingApproachTutorial** — Boarding

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipBoardingApproachTutorial** — Before you board an enemy ship, you must be close to them.{newline}{newline}Approach the enemy ship by using direct control.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipBoardingAttemptBoardingTutorial** — Boarding

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipBoardingAttemptBoardingTutorial** — To attempt boarding, turn your camera to an enemy ship which is close to your ship, and press {ATTEMPT_BOARDING_KEY}.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipBoardingTroopChargeTutorial** — Troop Orders

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipBoardingTroopChargeTutorial** — To give orders to your troops, select your own formation by pressing {FIRST_GROUP_HEAR_KEY} and select the order you want.{newline}{newline}Press {THIRD_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} to try “Charge” now!

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipBoardingTroopChargeTutorial_controller** — To give orders to your troops, open the formation selection by holding {HOLD_OPEN_ORDER_KEY} and select the order you want.{newline}{newline}Press {FIRST_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} and then {THIRD_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} to try “Charge” now!

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipCutLooseTutorial** — Cut Loose

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipCutLooseTutorial** — When your ship is connected to other ships, you can issue a cut loose order by pressing {CUT_LOOSE_KEY} while you are in direct control.

**str_campaign_tutorial_title.ShipCommandingShipsTutorial** — Commanding Friendly Ships

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipCommandingShipsTutorial** — You can command friendly ships, as long as you have the suitable authority.{newline}{newline}To command a ship to attack an enemy ship, press {SHIP_COMMANDING_TUTORIAL_GROUP_KEY} and then press {FOURTH_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} issue the engage order.

**str_campaign_tutorial_description.ShipCommandingShipsTutorial_controller** — You can command friendly ships, as long as you have the suitable authority.{newline}{newline}To command a ship to attack an enemy ship, hold {HOLD_OPEN_ORDER_KEY}, use the {SELECT_LEFT_FORMATION_KEY}/{SELECT_RIGHT_FORMATION_KEY} and {APPLY_SELECTION_KEY} to select an allied ship. Use {FIRST_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} to choose movement orders and press {FOURTH_ORDER_CATEGORY_KEY} issue the engage order.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.crewskeletal** — The minimum number of troops the ship can carry without travel speed penalties.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.crewdeck** — The number of troops the ship can carry into battle.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.cargo_capacity** — Inventory capacity the ship provides.{newline}{newline}Going above this limit will cause travel speed penalties.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.weight** — How heavy the ship is.{newline}{newline}Lighter ships are easier to maneuver and accelerate, but have more trouble in rough seas.{newline}{newline}Heavier ships are harder to accelerate, but handle rough seas better and deliver more devastating ramming attacks.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.travel_speed** — Travel speed of the ship.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.sail_type** — Sail type of the ship.{newline}{newline}Square sails provide higher acceleration, with moderate top speeds and limited wind coverage.{newline}{newline}Lateen sails provide low acceleration, with higher top speeds and wider wind coverage.{newline}{newline}Ships with both sail types have good acceleration, wind coverage and top speeds.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.draft_type** — Draft type of the ship.{newline}{newline}Ships with shallow drafts travel faster through rivers and coastal seas, and slower through open waters.{newline}{newline}Ships with deep drafts travel slower through rivers and coastal seas, and faster through open waters.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.sea_worthiness** — Resilience of the ship against the elements.{newline}{newline}Ships with high seaworthiness take less attrition on open sea, and can even handle light storms.

**str_ship_stat_explanation.hit_points** — Hit points of the ship.
