**str_board_game_title.Konane_0** — Setup

**str_board_game_title.Konane_1** — Moving and Capturing

**str_board_game_title.Konane_2** — Victory

**str_board_game_instruction.Konane_0** — The starting player chooses one of four pawns to be removed from the board.{newline}Then, the other player selects one of his adjacant pawns to also be removed. If the pawn of the starting player was in the center, the other player has to remove one of two pawns in the center too.{newline}{newline}The game now begins.

**str_board_game_instruction.Konane_1** — Moving pawns is only possible by capturing pawns from your opponent.{newline}Capturing is done by orthoginally jumping over 1 or more opposing pawns.

**str_board_game_instruction.Konane_2** — A player wins if his opponent can't make any more jumps (captures).

**str_board_game_title.Seega_0** — Setup

**str_board_game_title.Seega_1** — Movement

**str_board_game_title.Seega_2** — Capturing

**str_board_game_title.Seega_3** — Victory

**str_board_game_instruction.Seega_0** — Two pawns from each player start on the board as shown. Players take turns placing the rest on any available tile, excluding the center tile.

**str_board_game_instruction.Seega_1** — A pawn may be moved orthogonally, one tile at a time.{newline}A pawn can not be moved back to the tile that it came from in the previous turn.{newline}If a player is unable to move, that player may remove one of the opponent's pawns and still make a move.

**str_board_game_instruction.Seega_2** — Capture your opponent's pawns by surrounding them on both sides. If a pawn moves in between two opposing pawns, it does not get captured.{newline}In the first two images, white pawns get captured by the black pawns. In the last two, there are no captures.

**str_board_game_instruction.Seega_3** — A player wins if his opponent has only one or no pawns left.{newline}{newline}Another way to win is by constructing a barrier that has all of the pawns of the opposing player on one side. When a barrier has been constructed, the player with the most pawns left wins.

**str_board_game_title.Tablut_0** — Setup

**str_board_game_title.Tablut_1** — Movement

**str_board_game_title.Tablut_2** — Capturing

**str_board_game_title.Tablut_3** — Victory

**str_board_game_instruction.Tablut_0** — Tablut is a game of attackers (black) versus defenders (white).{newline}The attackers outnumber the defenders, but the defenders don't have to capture to win. Their main objective is to secure their king (center pawn).{newline}The king follows the same movement and capturing rules as the other pawns.

**str_board_game_instruction.Tablut_1** — Pawns can move to any tile in a vertical or horizontal direction, but they can never jump over other pawns.{newline}Pawns can not move on or over the center tile. Once the king leaves this tile, he can also no longer cross it.

**str_board_game_instruction.Tablut_2** — Capturing is done by surrounding an opposing pawn from both sides with your own pawns.{newline}Pawns can also be captured by blocking them against the center tile. This works for both players.

**str_board_game_instruction.Tablut_3** — The defenders win when they can move their king to any edge of the board.{newline}The attackers win when they capture the king, or if they can prevent all defenders from moving.

**str_board_game_title.Puluc_0** — Dice Roll

**str_board_game_title.Puluc_1** — Movement

**str_board_game_title.Puluc_2** — Capturing

**str_board_game_title.Puluc_3** — Back To Home

**str_board_game_title.Puluc_4** — Victory

**str_board_game_instruction.Puluc_0** — The starting player and the amount of tiles you can move each turn are decided by throwing four two-coloured sticks.

**str_board_game_instruction.Puluc_1** — Pawns travel toward the opponent's home-tile. Upon reaching the last tile, they will move back towards their own home-tile. Enemy pawns can be captured along the way.

**str_board_game_instruction.Puluc_2** — A pawn that lands on a tile with an opposing pawn already there, will capture that opposing pawn. The captured pawn will be stacked underneath the invading pawn.{newline}A stack of pawns can be also be re-captured as long as the top pawn belongs to the opponent.{newline}As soon as a pawn makes a capture, it will move back towards its home-tile in the next turn.

**str_board_game_instruction.Puluc_3** — When a stack lands exactly on its home-tile, all pawns of the player who controls the stack are returned to that player's hand, and can be re-used. The pawns belonging to the other player are eliminated from the game.

**str_board_game_instruction.Puluc_4** — A player wins if his opponent has no more available pawns in hand or on the board.

**str_board_game_title.BaghChal_0** — Setup

**str_board_game_title.BaghChal_1** — Movement

**str_board_game_title.BaghChal_2** — Capturing

**str_board_game_title.BaghChal_3** — Victory

**str_board_game_instruction.BaghChal_0** — Bagh Chal is a game of Sheep (white) versus Wolves (black).{newline}The wolves have four pawns that start on the four corners of the board. Every turn, one sheep is placed on the board, and one wolf makes a move or capture until all sheep have been placed on the board.{newline}After all sheep have been placed, the sheep can now also move on the board.

**str_board_game_instruction.BaghChal_1** — Wolves and sheep move in the same way by sliding along the lines on the board, one tile per turn.

**str_board_game_instruction.BaghChal_2** — Only wolves can capture, by jumping over a sheep to an available tile behind it. Capturing also follows the lines on the board.

**str_board_game_instruction.BaghChal_3** — The wolves win if they can remove 5 sheep from the board.{newline}{newline}The sheep win if they can block the wolves so they can't make any more moves.

**str_board_game_title.MuTorere_0** — Movement

**str_board_game_title.MuTorere_1** — Victory

**str_board_game_instruction.MuTorere_0** — You can only move a pawn that has an opposing pawn next to it, to the center tile.{newline}Every pawn can freely be moved one tile along the outer edge.{newline}A pawn on the center tile can move to any available tile.

**str_board_game_instruction.MuTorere_1** — A player wins if his opponent has been blocked and can no longer make any moves.

**str_ally_thanks_meet_after_helping_in_battle.0** — I don't think we have met properly my friend. You just saved my life out there, and I still don't know your name...

**str_ally_thanks_meet_after_helping_in_battle.1** — Your help was most welcome stranger. My name is {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}. Can I learn yours?

**str_ally_thanks_meet_after_helping_in_battle.2** — Thanks for your help, stranger. We haven't met properly yet, have we? What is your name?

**str_ally_thanks_after_helping_in_battle.0** — Well met indeed {PLAYER.LINK}. My name is {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK} and I am forever in your debt. If there is ever anything I can help you with, just let me know...

**str_ally_thanks_after_helping_in_battle.1** — Well met {PLAYER.LINK}. I am in your debt for what you just did. I hope one day I will find a way to repay it.

**str_ally_thanks_after_helping_in_battle.2** — Well met {PLAYER.LINK}. I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}. Thanks for your help and I hope we meet again.

**ally_thanks_after_helping_in_battle_has_met.0** — Again you save our necks, {PLAYER.LINK}! Truly, you are the best of friends.

**ally_thanks_after_helping_in_battle_has_met.1** — You arrived just in the nick of time! {PLAYER.LINK}. You have my deepest thanks!

**ally_thanks_after_helping_in_battle_has_met.2** — You turned up just in time, {PLAYER.LINK}. I will not forget your help.

**ally_thanks_after_helping_in_battle_has_met.3** — Good to see you here, {PLAYER.LINK}.

**str_townsfolk_asses_price_found** — Rumour has it the {ITEM_NAME} around here sells for cheaper than in other towns. If you were to buy some here and take it to {TOWN_NAME}, where it fetches a higher price, you could probably make around {PRICE_DIFF}{GOLD_ICON} of profit per item.

**str_townsfolk_asses_price_not_found** — Sorry, I don't know of any good trading tips at present.

**str_arena_reward** — If you can beat {OPPONENT_COUNT_1} opponents before going down, you'll earn {PRIZE_1}{GOLD_ICON}. You'll get {PRIZE_2}{GOLD_ICON} for striking down at least {OPPONENT_COUNT_2} opponents, {PRIZE_3}{GOLD_ICON} if you can defeat {OPPONENT_COUNT_3} opponents, and {PRIZE_4}{GOLD_ICON} if you can survive long enough to beat {OPPONENT_COUNT_4} opponents. If you can manage to be the last fighter standing, you'll earn the great prize of the fights, {PRIZE_5}{GOLD_ICON}. Sounds good, eh?[if:convo_nonchalant]

**str_arena_take_down.0** — Heh! That's quite the bruise you're sporting. But don't worry; everybody gets trounced once in a while. The important thing is to pick yourself up, dust yourself off and keep fighting. That's what champions do.

**str_arena_take_down.1** — Ha! Nothing like a good jab in the gut to let you know you're alive, eh? Looks like you managed to take down {OPPONENT_COUNT} opponents. Not bad. But that won't bring you any prize money. Now, if I were you, I would go back there and show everyone what I can do...

**str_arena_take_down.2** — You put up quite a good fight there. Some very good moves. A few errors, sure, but you definitely show promise. And you earned a prize of {PRIZE}{GOLD_ICON} for knocking down {OPPONENT_COUNT} opponents.

**str_arena_take_down.3** — Nice, {PLAYER.LINK}, nice. You managed to take down no less than {OPPONENT_COUNT} opponents. You were a crowd favorite, for your pluck. And of course, you earned a prize money of {PRIZE}{GOLD_ICON}.

**str_arena_take_down.4** — That was fine fighting, {PLAYER.LINK}. You took down {OPPONENT_COUNT} opponents. Of course you deserve a prize with that performance: {PRIZE}{GOLD_ICON}. Nice, eh?

**str_arena_take_down.5** — A magisterial performance, {PLAYER.LINK}. Whack! Crack! You took down {OPPONENT_COUNT} of them. The crowd loved it. And you earned a prize of {PRIZE}{GOLD_ICON}.

**str_arena_take_down.6** — Congratulations, champion! Your fight there was something to remember! As the last one standing, you of course win the top prize: {PRIZE}{GOLD_ICON}.

**str_robbery_threat.1** — Today's not your lucky day, friend. How about you hand over your silver? Be a real shame to have to cut anyone's throat.[if:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_robbery_threat.2** — Aye, what have we here? There's a tax for passage in these parts, traveler, paid either in coin or in blood.[if:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_robbery_threat.3** — Hello, traveler. Hope you brought your purse. See, we're what you might call brigands, and I'm afraid we can't let you pass without paying us a bit of coin.[if:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_robbery_threat.4** — You! Stop! Give us your silver. We're not playing games.[if:convo_angry]

**str_robbery_threat.5** — Stop right there. This is a robbery.[if:convo_aggressive]

**str_robbery_threat.6** — Hey - you. What you got in your bags? What are you carrying?[if:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_robbery_threat.forest_bandits_1** — Greetings, traveler. Welcome to our forest. We're going to have to collect a small toll.[rf:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_robbery_threat.forest_bandits_2** — Well now. Let's see what sort of fly has stumbled into our web.[rf:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_robbery_threat.sea_raiders_1** — Well there, traveller. We've just made landfall in these lands, hoping for a bit of luck with the raiding and pillaging, and aren't you a sight for sore eyes?[rf:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_robbery_threat.sea_raiders_2** — Stop there you dog! Show us what you've got!

**str_robbery_threat.desert_bandits_1** — Greetings, traveller. Unless you wish your bones to be left in the sand to be gnawed upon by jackals, give us what we want.

**str_robbery_threat.desert_bandits_2** — A hot day, is it not? Don't tire yourself fighting. Give us what we want and we'll leave.[rf:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_robbery_threat.steppe_bandits_1** — Stop there - easy now. The great eternal sky has given these lands to us. No one passes through here without our permission.

**str_robbery_threat.steppe_bandits_2** — Halt! Your foreign feet on this sacred land offend our ancestors. What are we going to do about that?[rf:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_robbery_threat.mountain_bandits_1** — Hello there, little lost sheep. We are wolves of the mountains, and we would like a moment of your time...[rf:convo_mocking_revenge]

**str_robbery_threat.mountain_bandits_2** — What have we here? Looks like the mountain spirits have answered our prayers, and granted us success in the hunt.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.1** — Oh, indeed we can, indeed we can. Provided you have a fat purse and are ready to lighten it, of course.[ib:hip][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.2** — Splendid. See, my lads and I, we're not cruel men. A bit greedy though, that can't be denied, so do be generous.[ib:hip][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.3** — Good, good. I much prefer a straight-up deal to rummaging through your gut afterward to see what you might have hid there.[ib:hip][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.4** — How much? How much money? Be quick.[ib:hip][rf:convo_angry]

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.5** — All right. So how much do you value your life?[ib:hip][if:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.6** — So how much are you going to give us?[rf:convo_angry]

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.sea_raiders_1** — Well then... It was a long voyage, so do dig deep into your purse.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.sea_raiders_2** — Arrr.. You'd best not be toying with us.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.forest_bandits_1** — Well, I'm glad you respect our ancient and sacred privileges.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.forest_bandits_2** — Wise little fly. How much?

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.desert_bandits_1** — That is wise of you.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.desert_bandits_2** — I am glad to hear that. Killing is thirsty work for us too.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.steppe_bandits_1** — Pay, and you may pass.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.steppe_bandits_2** — We will accept your offering.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.mountain_bandits_1** — Good. Sometimes it's better to shear the sheep than eat them.

**str_robbery_pay_agreement.mountain_bandits_2** — Make it worth our while not to kill you.

**str_robbery_conclusion.1** — Heh. You made a wise choice. Come back this way and we can do business again.[ib:closed][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_robbery_conclusion.2** — That'll do. For now, anyway. Travel safe - and I hope to see you again.[ib:closed][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_robbery_conclusion.3** — Good. Now be careful out there. World's full of thieves, not all of them as kind as we are.[ib:closed][rf:convo_bemused]

**str_robbery_conclusion.4** — Good! Good! Now go! Go away![ib:aggressive][if:convo_angry]

**str_robbery_conclusion.5** — We'll take it. You can live. Now go before I change my mind.[ib:closed][if:convo_normal]

**str_robbery_conclusion.6** — That's the spirit... We're a band of bastards that you really don't want to mess with.[rf:convo_bemused]

**str_robbery_conclusion.sea_raiders_1** — So kind you are, not sending us home empty-handed.

**str_robbery_conclusion.sea_raiders_2** — Now out of my sight, you mangy cringing cur!

**str_robbery_conclusion.forest_bandits_1** — Safe journeys! Don't let yourself get robbed by anyone but us!

**str_robbery_conclusion.forest_bandits_2** — Be on your way, little fly.

**str_robbery_conclusion.desert_bandits_1** — Be on your way. Safe journeys.

**str_robbery_conclusion.desert_bandits_2** — Good. Now be on your way. Don't forget to drink lots of water!

**str_robbery_conclusion.steppe_bandits_1** — You have our permission to proceed with your journey.

**str_robbery_conclusion.steppe_bandits_2** — You have acted wisely and with respect. You may go.

**str_robbery_conclusion.mountain_bandits_1** — Run along now, little sheep. And be careful of the other wolfpacks out there.

**str_robbery_conclusion.mountain_bandits_2** — Nice! No more sleeping on hard cold rock and dining on stringy squirrel.

**str_robbery_start_fight.1** — Mm. Pity.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_annoyed]

**str_robbery_start_fight.2** — Bad decision, friend.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_very_stern]

**str_robbery_start_fight.3** — Really? I suppose I'll be getting my hands dirty today, then.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_robbery_start_fight.4** — Right. You're dead.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_insulted]

**str_robbery_start_fight.5** — Afraid we'll need to make an example out of you, then. Don't bother begging for mercy.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_bared_teeth]

**str_robbery_start_fight.6** — You'll regret that answer.[ib:aggressive][if:convo_insulted]

**str_robbery_start_fight.forest_bandits_1** — Ah, I'm afraid we'll have to cut your throat then - on principle, of course. For trespassing.

**str_robbery_start_fight.forest_bandits_2** — A fly that wiggles and struggles a bit - we can handle that..

**str_robbery_start_fight.sea_raiders_1** — So be it... As my father says, a journey's not worthy of the name if you don't get to kill anyone.

**str_robbery_start_fight.sea_raiders_2** — Defy us, will you? We'll drink from your skull!

**str_robbery_start_fight.desert_bandits_1** — The jackals will feed well tonight, then.

**str_robbery_start_fight.desert_bandits_2** — We shall stain the sands with your blood, then.

**str_robbery_start_fight.steppe_bandits_1** — You shall be slain, then. Ready yourself.

**str_robbery_start_fight.steppe_bandits_2** — Very well - we shall cleanse this land with your blood.

**str_robbery_start_fight.mountain_bandits_1** — So you intend to fight, little sheep? Let's see your horns then.

**str_robbery_start_fight.mountain_bandits_2** — Hear that whistling and howling? That's not the wind - it's the ghosts of those who defied us. Prepare to join them.

**alley_street_fight_bet_result_1** — You bet {BET_AMOUNT} on yourself and you won the fight. Here is your reward {REWARD_AMOUNT}{GOLD_ICON}.

**alley_street_fight_bet_result_2** — You bet {BET_AMOUNT} on yourself but you have been defeated.

**alley_street_fight_bet_result_3** — You bet {BET_AMOUNT} on {FIGHTER_NAME} and {?FIGHTER_GENDER}she{?}he{\?} won the fight. Here is your reward {REWARD_AMOUNT}{GOLD_ICON}.

**alley_street_fight_bet_result_4** — You bet {BET_AMOUNT} on {FIGHTER_NAME} but {?FIGHTER_GENDER}she{?}he{\?} has been defeated.

**str_culture_description.vlandia** — The Vlandians are the descendants of adventurers from the west who lived under the Empire for centuries before forming an independent kingdom. With the decline of imperial authority, they have evolved into a well organised feudal society led by a caste of warlike nobles who prefer to fight with spears and lances on horseback.

**str_culture_description.battania** — The Battanians still remember the olden days when the woods stretched across northern Calradia, and the Empire and its cities had yet to violate their sanctity. The fierce warriors remain loyal to their traditional ways. They paint their faces when going to battle and even their noblemen prefer to fight on foot while using great axes and two-handed swords with deadly efficiency.

**str_culture_description.khuzait** — The Khuzait confederation of steppe tribes used to live a nomadic life, but have recently settled in the eastern frontier of the Empire and are slowly transitioning into an agrarian society with permanent town centers. Despite this, they still retain many aspects of their nomadic life, including their affinity with horses. They are masters of mounted archery, shooting and then galloping out of reach.

**str_culture_description.sturgia** — Sturgians are the descendants of the foreign tribes of northern Calradia. As the empire expanded into their cold forests, they found a ready market for the luxurious furs of woodland animals whom they traditionally hunted and trapped. Sturgian chieftains became princes, vying for pre-eminence with the help of Nord mercenaries who migrated into their realm. They are good hunters and wanderers, travelling far in search of opportunities both for trade and for plunder.

**str_culture_description.aserai** — The Aserai are the inhabitants of the Nahasa desert, a mixture of nomadic bedouin and settled oasis farmers. They are famous for their horsemanship and their knowledge of the learning of many lands, especially medicine, gained from lying on some of the continent's most lucrative trade routes. Each clan is fiercely proud of its lineage and often jealous of the others, but when united by a charismatic leader, they become a major force in the south.

**str_culture_description.empire** — The Calradian Empire is in decline. Even before the suspicious death of the Emperor Arenicos, the once united realm was torn by political rivalries. Today, those factions are in open war. Yet Calradians endure. Their methodical study of defensive strategy, in which garrison cities slow down invading forces until mobile field armies can come to their rescue, helps hold their neighbors at bay.

**str_settlement_rebellion.0** — This region is gripped by civil disorder, yet people must still go about their daily chores. For the most part, they not linger long in the markets or make eye contact. But you overhear hushed conversations about the rebels in the countryside. Some seem to be afraid of the rebels, others secretly thrilled that the tables have turned, even for a little while, on the rich and powerful.

**str_town_long_prosperity_1.Low** — The town is clearly going through hard times. People look malnourished and buildings are poorly maintained.

**str_town_long_prosperity_1.Mid** — The town is of average wealth.

**str_town_long_prosperity_1.High** — The town is prosperous. The people look well-fed and relatively comfortable.

**str_companion_added** — {COMPANION.NAME} joined your party.

**str_village_long_prosperity.Low** — The village is going through hard times. Farm tools are rusty and broken. Brush and weeds are reclaiming the outermost fields.

**str_village_long_prosperity.Mid** — The village is of average wealth. Humans and animals alike look well-fed. Villagers busily attend to the tasks of the seasons.

**str_village_long_prosperity.High** — The village is prosperous. Brimming sacks of grain, healthy animals and loaded carts testify to the bounty of the fields.

**str_settlement_morale_high_prosperity** — You hear much praise for the wisdom of the rulers who have achieved this prosperity.

**str_settlement_morale_high_average** — You hear few complaints and people seem to have confidence in the authorities.

**str_settlement_morale_high_adversity** — Despite the hardship, you hear few murmurs of complaint, and people seem to trust their rulers to lead them through adversity.

**str_settlement_morale_medium_prosperity** — Mostly people are content, although you hear some complaints about rising prices, the unequal distribution of wealth, and migrants coming from the countryside.

**str_settlement_morale_medium_average** — You hear some complaints about prices, shortages and greedy merchants, but no more than normal.

**str_settlement_morale_medium_adversity** — Despite the poverty, you hear few words of complaint, as though people are too beaten down to expect any change.

**str_settlement_morale_rebellious_prosperity** — Yet the prosperity is clearly not benefiting everyone equally. People seem angry, complaining endlessly about new rural migrants, rising prices, and those who are profiting more than others.

**str_settlement_morale_rebellious_average** — Though it seems most people are managing to get by, many seem angry, and you overhear a few passers-by muttering that their patience is giving out. You sense something may be stirring.

**str_settlement_morale_rebellious_adversity** — People openly curse the authorities, as though they feel they have nothing to lose.

**str_settlement_rebellious_state** — Settlement is rebelling.

**str_options_description.Language** — Your preferred game language.

**str_options_description.VoiceLanguage** — Your preferred voice over language.

**str_options_description.MasterVolume** — Master volume level.

**str_options_description.MusicVolume** — Music volume level.

**str_options_description.VoiceOverVolume** — Voice-over volume level.

**str_options_description.VoiceChatVolume** — Voice chat volume level.

**str_options_description.SoundVolume** — Sound effects volume level.

**str_options_description.SoundDevice** — Your preferred sound output device.

**str_options_description.MaxSimultaneousSoundEventCount** — How many sounds could be played at once. Lower values will lower your CPU usage while higher values delivers better atmosphere.

**str_options_description.KeepSoundInBackground** — Keep game sounds while game is out of focus.

**str_options_description.SoundOcclusion** — Muffles the sound sources behind obstacles. Forced ON in Multiplayer.

**str_options_description.SoundPreset** — You can switch between different mix modes better suited to your liking.

**str_options_description.SoundOutput** — Change the sound output method to one most fitting for your speaker configuration.

**str_options_description.MouseSensitivity** — Set sensitivity for cursor movement and camera control.

**str_options_description.InvertMouseYAxis** — Invert Y Axis for camera control. (Does not work on campaign map.)

**str_options_description.MouseYMovementScale** — Set your vertical movement multiplier for direction gestures, compared to horizontal movement. Does not affect camera movement.

**str_options_description.TrailAmount** — Set thickness for trails of weapons.

**str_options_description.EnableVibration** — Enable the controller vibration effect.

**str_options_description.ControlBlockDirection** — Choose how to perform blocks. Auto will default to "By Look Direction" in Multiplayer.

**str_options_description.ControlAttackDirection** — Choose how to perform attacks.

**str_options_description.CombatAI** — Select how challenging the combat AI will be.

**str_options_description.CampaignAI** — Campaign AI DESC

**str_options_description.CombatSpeed** — Combat Speed DESC

**str_options_description.BattleSize** — Sets the maximum number of units on battles. A higher value requires better CPU and GPU.

**str_options_description.ReinforcementWaveCount** — Sets the number of reinforcement waves that will be spawned in a combat mission. A higher value generally means longer mission duration. On settings lower than unlimited, sieges might be resolved without all troops participating in the fight.

**str_options_description.TurnCameraWithHorseInFirstPerson** — Turn camera as you change direction on a horse in first person view.

**str_options_description.ShowAttackDirection** — Enable marks for direction of attack.

**str_options_description.ShowTargetingReticle** — Enable crosshair for ranged weapons.

**str_options_description.AutoSaveInterval** — Sets the interval of time between autosaves. Value is in minutes.

**str_options_description.FriendlyTroopsBannerOpacity** — Determines the opacity of the banners shown on top of the friendly troops.

**str_options_description.AlwaysShowFriendlyTroopBannersType** — When enabled, friendly troops banner indicators are always shown, not only while holding the Show Indicators key.

**str_options_type_AlwaysShowFriendlyTroopBannersType_0** — Disabled

**str_options_type_AlwaysShowFriendlyTroopBannersType_1** — Multiplayer Only

**str_options_type_AlwaysShowFriendlyTroopBannersType_2** — Enabled

**str_options_description.ShowFormationDistances** — Enable formation distance texts. When disabled, formation icons will scale to indicate distances.

**str_options_description.ReportDamage** — Enable text reports for damage dealt.

**str_options_description.ReportBark** — Enable text reports for shouts.

**str_options_description.EnableTutorialHints** — Enable informative messages.

**str_options_description.ReportPersonalDamage** — Enable interface elements that report players damage and casualities in center bottom.

**str_options_description.ReportCasualtiesType** — Enable reports for deaths and knock outs.

**str_options_description.CombatCameraDistance** — Determines how far will the camera be in third-person.

**str_options_description.ReportExperience** — Enable reports for experience gain.

**str_options_description.StopGameOnFocusLost** — Stop the game when the focus is lost to the game window.

**str_options_description.SlowDownOnOrder** — Enable slowing down the game while the player is giving orders.

**str_options_description.ClothSimulation** — Enables the cloth simulation. Uses GPU resources.

**str_options_description.InteractiveGrass** — Enables the deformable grass.

**str_options_description.OverAll** — Sets the overall graphics quality preset.

**str_options_description.ScreenResolution** — Sets the resolution of the game. Higher resolution requires a more powerful display adapter.

**str_options_description.RefreshRate** — Sets the refresh rate of the game.

**str_options_description.ResolutionScale** — Sets the resolution scale. Lower values can increase performance. {newline}{newline}Uses AMD's "FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0"{newline}{newline}Does not affect UI Quality

**str_options_description.FrameLimiter** — Sets the frame limiter.

**str_options_description.Antialiasing** — Sets the anti-aliasing technique.

**str_options_description.DLSS** — Sets the NVIDIA DLSS method if applicable.

**str_options_description.Occlusion** — Sets the ambient occlusion technique.

**str_options_description.Benchmark** — Start the Bannerlord Benchmark.

**str_options_description.Brightness** — Calibrate contrast levels.

**str_options_description.ExposureCompensation** — Set the exposure amount.

**str_options_description.SharpenAmount** — Sets the amount of sharpen effect.

**str_options_description.ShadowmapResolution** — Sets the resolution of shadows.

**str_options_description.ShadowmapType** — Sets the type of shadows.

**str_options_description.ShadowmapFiltering** — Sets the shadow filtering technique.

**str_options_description.ParticleDetail** — Sets the quality of particles. A higher value means more detailed particles.

**str_options_description.ParticleQuality** — Sets the render quality of particles. A higher value means sharper particles.

**str_options_description.TextureBudget** — Affects the size of the texture streaming cache. A higher value requires more video memory but provides a smoother experience.

**str_options_description.TextureQuality** — Affects the quality of textures.

**str_options_description.ShaderQuality** — Sets the quality of shaders. A higher value means better graphical effects.

**str_options_description.Bloom** — Enables the bloom effect.

**str_options_description.DepthOfField** — Enables the depth of field.

**str_options_description.SunShafts** — Enables the sun shafts.

**str_options_description.MotionBlur** — Enables the motion blur.

**str_options_description.SSSSS** — Enables the subsurface scattering.

**str_options_description.SSR** — Enables the screen space reflections.

**str_options_description.Tesselation** — Enables the tesselation.

**str_options_description.FoliageQuality** — Sets the quality of trees and grass.

**str_options_description.CharacterDetail** — Sets the detail level of character models.

**str_options_description.NumberOfCorpses** — Sets the number of visible corpses.

**str_options_description.NumberOfRagDolls** — Sets the number of simultaneous ragdoll simulations.

**str_options_description.AnimationSamplingQuality** — Affects the animation sampling frame rate. A higher value requires more CPU resource but provides smoother animations.

**str_options_description.ShowBlood** — Choose whether blood is visible in battles.

**str_options_description.TextureFiltering** — Sets the texture filtering technique. A higher value means more detailed and sharp textures.

**str_options_description.DisplayMode** — Sets the window mode.{newline}Windowed: Runs the game on a window.{newline}Fullscreen: Runs the game in full screen.{newline}Borderless Fullscreen: Runs the game on a borderless maximized window.

**str_options_description.SelectedMonitor** — Sets the monitor that the game window will be displayed.

**str_options_description.SelectedAdapter** — Sets the display adapter that the game will run on.

**str_options_description.VSync** — Synchronizes the game to the monitor's refresh rate. Eliminates tearing artifacts.

**str_options_description.GraphicsMode** — Sets the graphics mode.{newline}Performance: Runs the game at 60 frames per second with dynamic resolution, lower quality settings and less units on battles.{newline}Fidelity: Runs the game at 30 frames per second at the native resolution, higher quality settings and more units on battles.

**str_options_description.OneTwentyHzMode** — Locks the framerate to 40 Hz on the Fidelity Mode and unlocks it on the Performance Mode.

**str_options_description.DynamicResolution** — Allow the render resolution to be scaled down to maintain the targeted frame rate.{newline}{newline}Uses AMD's "FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0"{newline}{newline}Does not affect UI Quality

**str_options_description.DynamicResolutionTarget** — Target framerate to be maintained by the "Dynamic Resolution Scaling" setting.{newline}{newline}It is advised that you set it to the lowest framerate you're comfortable playing with. Setting a value that's too high will cause unnecessary resolution drops.

**str_options_description.FSR** — Enables AMD FidelityFX™ Super Resolution.

**str_options_description.PhysicsTickRate** — Sets the dynamic physics simulation frame rate. A higher value requires more CPU resource but provides smoother physics simulation.

**str_options_description.FilmGrain** — Enables the film grain.

**str_options_description.LightingQuality** — Sets the lighting quality.

**str_options_description.EnvironmentDetail** — Sets the detail level of environment props.

**str_options_description.TerrainQuality** — Sets the terrain quality.

**str_options_description.DecalQuality** — Sets the decal quality.

**str_options_description.WaterQuality** — Sets the quality of water. A higher value means more detailed water simulation.

**str_options_description.SSRQuality** — Sets the quality of screen space reflections. A higher value means more detailed reflection.

**str_options_description.EnableDamageTakenVisuals** — Enable the red border around the screen when the player takes damage.

**str_options_description.ForceVSyncInMenus** — Force VSync in Menus (i.e. Lobby, Inventory, Party, Character, Quest etc.)

**str_options_description.EnableVerticalAimCorrection** — Enable vertical aim correction while in third person mode.

**str_options_description.ZoomSensitivityModifier** — Set how much the sensitivity changes when the camera is zoomed in.

**str_options_description.CrosshairType** — Crosshair that shows when using a ranged weapon.

**str_options_description.EnableGenericAvatars** — Show generic avatars for players. This will replace all of the players' avatars with generic avatars.

**str_options_description.EnableGenericNames** — Show generic names for players. This will replace all of the players' names with generic names.

**str_options_description.OrderType** — Order visuals that are visible while giving orders in battles.

**str_options_description.OrderLayoutType** — Choose the layout of orders (i.e. order categories and keys){newline}Default: The default order layout.{newline}Legacy: The order layout used in the earlier versions of the game.

**str_options_description.UnitSpawnPrioritization** — Determine unit spawn prioritization.{newline}Default: Units spawn according to their position in the party roster.{newline}High Level: High level units will spawn first.{newline}Low Level: Low level units will spawn first.{newline}Homogeneous: Spawn units homogeneously based on their troop types rather than their levels. This option will try to fill the ranks with each type of unit at the same ratio and ignore their tiers while doing it.{newline}The settings above apply only to the player's starting composition. The AI is not affected.

**str_options_description.EnableVoiceChat** — Enable incoming voice chat messages from players in your team.

**str_options_description.EnableDeathIcon** — Enable death location indicators that show where your teammates die.

**str_options_description.AutoTrackAttackedSettlements** — Enable auto tracking settlements when attacked.

**str_options_description.EnableNetworkAlertIcons** — Enable network alert icons.{newline}1. Latency{newline}2. Packet Loss{newline}3. Poor Server Performance

**str_options_description.HideBattleUI** — Hides battle UI elements while the player is in a mission.

**str_options_description.EnableSingleplayerChatBox** — Enable event log in campaign map and missions.

**str_options_description.EnableMultiplayerChatBox** — Enable chat log.

**str_options_description.PlayerReceivedDamageDifficulty** — Determines the damage received by your character.

**str_options_description.MapDoubleClickBehavior** — Determines how the map time controls behave on a double click.{newline}Default: Regular play mode on single click, fast forward on double click.{newline}Alternative: Double click to toggle between regular play and fast forward modes.{newline}Disabled: Double click works the same as single click, time control mode must be changed manually.

**str_brightness_option_explainer** — If the checkered patterns are not visible inside the frames, try moving the sliders.{newline}Adjust the sliders to the point where patterns are barely visible.

**str_exposure_option_explainer** — Adjust the exposure level according to your preference using the slider.
